description: Keyboard focus lands on header links (logo, nav, EN/FR, Menu) while the header is translated off-screen (yPercent -110) after scrolling down; focused element is invisible (audit: inView false, y=-55).

description: Auto-advancing slides (every 4–8s, indefinitely) have no pause mechanism and their caption is aria-live=polite, so screen readers announce a new caption every few seconds while the user reads elsewhere (WCAG 2.2.2, 4.1.3 noise).
suggested_fix: Pause autoplay while the pointer is over or focus is inside the slides, stop autoplay after the user picks a tab, and only make the caption live when the user changed the slide.

description: Inactive slide tab labels (text-paper/45, 0.6rem ≈ 9.6px) fail contrast (axe color-contrast serious).
suggested_fix: Raise to text-paper/65 (≥4.5:1 on ink).

description: Preview window title bar truncates the slug ('WHATSAPP-AI-AGE…') because the traffic-light dots + badge leave too little room on phones.
suggested_fix: Hide the decorative dots below sm so slug and badge both fit.

description: With the mobile menu open, the page behind is not inert: Tab moves past the 4 menu links into hidden page content under the full-screen overlay.
suggested_fix: Set inert on #main and footer while the menu is open.

description: Copy email gives no feedback when navigator.clipboard is missing (plain-http LAN preview, older browsers) or writeText rejects; rapid repeated clicks let an old timer hide 'Copied' early.
suggested_fix: Fallback to a hidden textarea + execCommand('copy'); clear the previous timer on each click.

description: Hero eyebrow wraps to a lone 'UNIVERSITY' on the second line at 375px (orphan).
suggested_fix: text-balance on the eyebrow line so the two lines are even.

description: Unknown URLs (/de, /en/anything) show Next's default white '404 | This page could not be found' page: off-brand next to the dark site and a dead end with no link back.
suggested_fix: app/global-not-found.tsx (root layout is under [locale]) with the site's styles and links to /en and /fr; enable experimental.globalNotFound.

viewport: all (verified 1440 and 375, en; same code path in fr)
description: In full-motion mode (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, which is what most keyboard and screen-reader users have), none of the Contact controls can be reached with Tab until the visitor has scrolled the section into view. Every [data-reveal] wrapper starts as visibility:hidden (CSS, before hydration) and GSAP autoAlpha:0 keeps it that way until its ScrollTrigger fires. visibility:hidden elements cannot take focus. Measured on a fresh load: el.focus() fails on the mailto link, Copy, Download CV, LinkedIn and GitHub (5 of 5; computed visibility 'hidden'). Tabbing forward from the last Projects control ('VIEW WEBSITE ↗') goes straight to the footer's 'BACK TO TOP ↑' and skips all five, both at 1440 and at 375. Scrolling to the footer only then fires the reveal, after focus has already passed. The screen-reader tree for #contact at that point is just the h2: the intro paragraph, email, CV and social links are all missing. These are the page's main calls to action. Fails WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard (A), 2.4.3 Focus Order (A) and 1.3.1 (A). The existing audit missed it because capture.mjs prime() scrolls the whole page before the keyboard and axe passes.
suggested_fix: Never use visibility:hidden as the pre-reveal state. Change the CSS to `html.js [data-reveal]{opacity:0}` and animate `opacity` (not `autoAlpha`) in Reveals.tsx (default: fromTo {opacity:0,y:40} → {opacity:1,y:0}; stagger: from children {opacity:0,y:32}). Content then stays in the accessibility tree and focusable. Also add a `focusin` listener on each [data-reveal] (or document-level) that calls `tween.progress(1)` / `scrollTrigger.kill()` so a focused, still-transparent element becomes visible at once (2.4.7).
verified_evidence: shots/contact/p1-fix/1440-tab-to-email-fresh-load.png; verify-reveal: fresh-load Tab reaches email/Copy/CV/LinkedIn/GitHub, 0 visibility:hidden controls

description: In full-motion mode, a screen reader gets an empty Experience section until the visitor has visually scrolled past it. On a fresh load, 38 of 40 checked nodes in #experience have computed visibility:hidden: the 'Experience' label, the 'Work 04' and 'Education 02' labels and all 6 <li> rows (data-reveal on each li). ariaSnapshot of #experience is only `heading "What I've done so far." [level=2]`, then `list` and `list` with no items. With VoiceOver or NVDA in browse mode, the reading cursor skips from the h2 to the next visible node, so all work and education history is lost unless the page happens to scroll far enough to trigger each row's 'top 88%' reveal first. The h2 itself uses the 'lines' reveal (set visible immediately) and stays readable, which makes the gap harder to notice. Fails 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (A) in effect (content missing from the accessibility tree) and 1.3.2.
suggested_fix: Same root fix as the contact finding: pre-reveal state = opacity:0 (plus transform), never visibility:hidden or autoAlpha. That keeps rows exposed to AT while they fade in visually.
note: same root fix as contact P0 (opacity-only reveals)

description: In full-motion mode, the Skills section is exposed to screen readers as a heading followed by three empty lists. On a fresh load, 17 of 22 checked nodes are visibility:hidden: the 'Skills' label, the intro paragraph, the three group titles (Languages, Foundations, AI) and all 11 chips. The <ul data-reveal="stagger"> is made visible, but Reveals.tsx then sets autoAlpha:0 on every child <li>. ariaSnapshot of #skills is `heading "The toolkit."`, then `list`, `list`, `list` with zero items. A screen-reader user in browse mode hears 'list, 0 items' three times and none of the skills.
suggested_fix: In the stagger case, animate `opacity` and `y` on the children instead of `autoAlpha`, and change the global pre-state to opacity:0. That keeps the list items in the accessibility tree.

description: 'Back to top' scrolls the page but leaves keyboard focus where it was. Measured: after pressing Enter on the button and waiting 2.6 s, scrollY = 0 but document.activeElement is still the footer button at y ≈ 15802 px (off-screen). The next Tab goes to <body> (end of the document), then to the browser UI or back to the skip link. A keyboard or screen-reader user sees the top of the page while their focus is stranded at the bottom, and a screen reader keeps reading from the footer. Fails 2.4.3 Focus Order (A) and 2.4.7 (the focused element isn't visible).
suggested_fix: After scrollToTarget(0), move focus to the top of the page with preventScroll so the smooth scroll isn't interrupted: e.g. give #main or the hero h1 tabIndex={-1} and call `el.focus({preventScroll:true})`. Or make the control an <a href="#top"> that Lenis intercepts, and focus the target in the same way.
verified_evidence: verify-bottom back-to-top: active=main, next Tab = View projects

description:
The row DOM order puts the dates before the heading: then

org

, role/place, description. A screen-reader user moving by heading (H key / rotor), the most common way to scan a CV-style list, lands on 'AGBU Montreal' and reads forward through role, place and description, but never hears that row's dates. They sit before the heading, so they get read as trailing text of the previous row (e.g. '…kept coming back. 2025 — 2026' then heading 'Independent Tutoring'). The ariaSnapshot confirms each listitem starts with a bare `text: Jul — Sep 2026` above the heading. Fails 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence (A) and 1.3.1.
suggested_fix:
Put the

first in the DOM and the dates after it, and restore the visual order with grid placement (e.g. dates `md:col-start-1 md:row-start-1`, heading block `md:col-start-4`, or `order-first` on mobile). Or wrap the dates in

directly under the h3. Mark the dates up as .
note: h4 first in DOM, dates order-first / lg grid placement

description:
The group titles 'Work' / 'Education' ('Expérience' / 'Formation' in fr) are plain

elements, and the two

    lists have no accessible name. Heading outline: h2 'What I've done so far.' → six h3 rows with nothing that separates work from education. Heading navigation can't tell the McGill and Collège rows (education) apart from the jobs, and list navigation announces 'list, 4 items' / 'list, 2 items' with no label. The visual structure (two labelled groups) is not conveyed programmatically. Fails 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (A).
suggested_fix: Render the group title as <h3 id=...> (styled the same) and bump the org names to <h4>, or at least add `aria-labelledby` on each <ol> pointing at the title span.
note: group titles are h3 labelling their ol, orgs h4

description:
The skill group titles (Languages / Foundations / AI; Langages / Fondamentaux / IA) are

elements, and the

    chip lists aren't linked to them. The Skills section has a single h2 and no sub-headings. Screen-reader users jumping by list (L key / rotor) hear 'list, 4 items, Python…' with no group name. The 'AI' list (Claude Code, ChatGPT, Codex, Gemini) is only understandable if you happen to read the preceding paragraph. Fails 1.3.1 (A).
suggested_fix: Use <h3 id={`skills-${i}`} className="label-mono …"> for the group title and `<ul aria-labelledby={`skills-${i}`}>`.

description: The marquee band moves on its own for as long as it's on screen (a 30 s loop, repeat:-1), with no way to pause, stop or hide it. It also speeds up to 7× base speed with scroll velocity (target = 1 + min(6, v/250)) and reverses direction on scroll-up. aria-hidden hides it from screen readers but not from sighted users with vestibular or attention disorders. The only escape is the OS-level prefers-reduced-motion setting. 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (A) requires a mechanism for moving content that lasts more than 5 s alongside other content. Relying on the platform setting is arguable at best, and the velocity boost makes it worse (2.3.3 Animation from Interactions, AAA).
suggested_fix: Pause the loop on hover and on focus-within of the section, and offer a small visible pause/play toggle (or stop the drift after a few seconds and only move with scroll). Cap the scroll boost at around 2×.
note: marquee eases to a stop under the mouse

description: The Copy button's live region sits inside the button (). Activating it changes the button's own accessible name from 'Copy' to 'Copied ✓' (ariaSnapshot after Enter: `button "Copied ✓"`) and fires a polite announcement at the same time. Screen readers differ here: VoiceOver often reads the name change and the live region, so you hear it twice, while some NVDA/JAWS versions drop live updates inside the focused control. After 1.8 s the text reverts, and the live region announces a spurious 'Copy' (ariaSnapshot after revert: `button "Copy"`). The status message is unreliable and noisy (4.1.3 Status Messages, AA).
suggested_fix: Keep the button's name stable (e.g. aria-label or visible text 'Copy email'). Render a separate visually-hidden `<span role="status" aria-live="polite">` outside the button, and set it to 'Email copied' on success. Clear it silently: set it to '' before the next message instead of announcing 'Copy'. The visual '✓' swap can stay, marked aria-hidden.

description: The Copy control is visually indistinguishable from the static 'EMAIL' label beside it (same label-mono, text-mute #8a8f98, 11.5 px). The only thing that marks it as a button is its pill border, color-line #2a2d33 on ink #0b0c0e = 1.42:1, well below the 3:1 that 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (AA) requires for the visual information that identifies a UI component. The LinkedIn / GitHub .btn borders are also 1.42:1, but their paper text (16.4:1) and button padding make them more recognisable. The problem is sharpest on Copy.
suggested_fix: Give the Copy button a border of at least 3:1 against ink (e.g. border-mute #8a8f98 = 6.0:1, or trace-plus, around #5a5f68 ≈ 3.0:1), and/or paper text so it reads as a control. Consider the same border bump for .btn.
note: Copy text now paper/80 so the label, not the 1.4:1 border, identifies the control

description: LinkedIn and GitHub open in a new tab (target="_blank"), and the only cue is the '↗' glyph, which is aria-hidden. Sighted users get the hint; screen-reader users hear just 'link, LinkedIn' and are then dropped into a new tab or window with the Back button disabled. The information is conveyed visually but not programmatically (1.3.1). Also advisory technique G201 and 3.2.5 Change on Request (AAA).
suggested_fix: Keep the ↗ aria-hidden but add a visually-hidden suffix, e.g. `{locale==='fr' ? ' (nouvel onglet)' : ' (opens in a new tab)'}`, or drop target=_blank.

description: The footer clock re-renders every second forever (setInterval 1000 ms), including when prefers-reduced-motion is set (measured 17:29:17 → 17:29:18 in the reduced-motion context). There is no pause or hide. It is auto-updating content presented in parallel with other content, which is what 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (A) covers, and the seconds digit is a constant flicker in peripheral vision. It is correctly not aria-live, but some screen readers refresh the virtual buffer on DOM mutation and may reset or re-read around it. The server-rendered and no-JS content is the literal '--:--:--', which is read as 'dash dash colon dash dash colon dash dash' and is not valid <time> content. There is no datetime attribute.
suggested_fix: Show HH:MM and tick once a minute (aligned to the minute boundary). That removes the moving seconds and 59 of every 60 DOM mutations. Render nothing, or aria-hide the placeholder, until mounted. Add `dateTime` with the ISO time. Optionally stop updating under prefers-reduced-motion.
note: reduced motion shows HH:MM (no ticking seconds)

description: The Copy pill changes shape on keyboard focus. The global `:focus-visible { border-radius: 2px }` is unlayered CSS, so it beats Tailwind v4's `rounded-full`, which lives in @layer utilities. The measured computed radius goes from 3.35544e+07px (pill) to 2px on focus, so the control turns into a sharp rectangle inside a square ring. The same happens to every Tailwind-rounded focusable on the page. .btn keeps its pill only because its unlayered `.btn{border-radius:999px}` comes later in the file.
suggested_fix: Remove `border-radius` from the global :focus-visible rule (outlines follow the element's own radius in current browsers), or move the rule into `@layer base` so utilities win.
verified_evidence: verify-bottom copy radius stays pill on focus

description: The '↑' in 'Back to top ↑' / 'Haut de page ↑' is part of the button's accessible name (ariaSnapshot: `button "Back to top ↑"`), so screen readers say 'Back to top, upwards arrow'. This is inconsistent with Contact and Hero, where the ↓ / ↗ glyphs are wrapped in aria-hidden spans.
suggested_fix: `{t(footer.backToTop, locale)} ↑`

description: The Copy button's name, 'Copy' / 'Copier', doesn't say what it copies. It only makes sense from visual proximity to the email, and screen-reader users tabbing (link, then button) hear just 'Copy, button'. The success state 'Copied ✓' also reads the glyph aloud ('Copied check mark'). This is 2.4.6 Headings and Labels (AA) in the weak sense, and a best practice.
suggested_fix: Add aria-label 'Copy email address' / 'Copier l'adresse courriel' (the visible 'Copy' is contained in the name, so 2.5.3 still passes), and wrap ✓ in aria-hidden.

description: The 'Download CV' / 'Télécharger le CV' link (download attribute, /cv/Gregory_Sutjian_CV.pdf) doesn't state the file type or size. Screen-reader users hear 'link, Download CV' and get an unannounced file download (2.4.4 advisory: identify non-HTML targets).
suggested_fix: Add a visually-hidden ' (PDF, 120 KB)' or a small visible 'PDF' tag inside the link.

description: The Copy button is only 60×30 CSS px on touch viewports (audit smallTargets). That passes 2.5.8 Target Size Minimum (24 px, AA), but it's well under the 44 px of 2.5.5 (AAA) and the platform guidance. At 375 it sits 12 px (gap-y-3) under the multi-line mailto link, so a miss opens the mail app instead of copying.
suggested_fix: Add the existing `tap-area` class, or py-3 on coarse pointers (`pointer-coarse:py-3`), to reach 44 px without changing the look.

description: The email link uses `break-all`, so at 320 px (the 1.4.10 Reflow width) the address splits mid-token as 'gregory.sutjian@mail.mcgil' / 'l.ca'. With 1.4.12 text-spacing overrides at 375 it splits as 'mcgi' / 'll.ca'. Nothing is lost, but low-vision and dyslexic users copying the address by eye can misread it.
suggested_fix: Use `[overflow-wrap:anywhere]` with a `<wbr/>` before '@' and before 'mail.', so it breaks at meaningful points ('gregory.sutjian' / '@mail.mcgill.ca').

description: The role/place separator is a real text '/' in text-line #2a2d33 on ink, measured at 1.42:1. It fails 1.4.3's 4.5:1 if treated as text, and screen readers read it aloud ('Math Tutor slash Montreal', 'Tuteur en mathématiques barre oblique Montréal'). It is either meaningful, in which case it is too faint, or decorative, in which case it shouldn't be spoken.
suggested_fix: `/,`, or raise it to text-mute (6.0:1).

description: The zero-padded counters next to the group titles ('Work 04', 'Education 02', 'Expérience 04') are read aloud as part of the label ('Work zero four'). They duplicate what the <ol> already announces ('list, 4 items'). The date ranges use an em dash with abbreviations ('Jul — Sep 2026', 'févr. — mai 2024'). VoiceOver's default punctuation level drops the em dash ('Jul Sep 2026'), which loses the 'to' meaning, and there's no machine-readable <time>.
suggested_fix: aria-hidden the counter span. Wrap dates as `Jul — to Sep 2026`, or provide an sr-only range string.

description: None of the bottom sections is exposed as a landmark. <section id="experience">, #skills and #contact have no aria-labelledby or aria-label, so browsers map them to generic rather than region. The 'In one sentence' statement section is labelled, so the page is inconsistent. Landmark navigation (VoiceOver rotor / NVDA D) shows only header, nav, main and contentinfo.
suggested_fix: Give each section's h2 an id and add `aria-labelledby` on the <section> (SectionHeader can take an id prop).

description: The skill chips are static <li> elements, but on hover they look interactive: the border turns copper, a copper glow appears and the side 'pins' light up. Users with cognitive or low-vision needs may try to click them, and nothing happens. The affordance doesn't match the role (hovering over non-controls is a common confusion source under 3.2 Predictable, best practice).
suggested_fix: Tone the hover down to a subtle, non-button change, e.g. only the pins light up with no border or glow change, or drop it entirely.
note: hover lighting is the site-wide circuit motif; now gated to hover-capable pointers so touch never sees it

description: In Windows High Contrast / forced-colors mode, the decorative outline name 'SUTJIAN' (color: transparent + 1px text-stroke) has its transparent fill forced to CanvasText. It renders as a solid 17.5vw block of text that dominates the footer. It is aria-hidden, so this is purely visual clutter for forced-colors users. Also in forced colors, the marquee outline words become solid, which is acceptable.
suggested_fix: `@media (forced-colors: active){ .footer-mark{ forced-color-adjust:none; color:transparent; -webkit-text-stroke-color:GrayText } }` (or display:none).

description: The FR contact heading overflows the chip box and gets clipped at the screen edge. The h2 is clamp(3rem,8.2vw,…), so it bottoms out at 48px. At that size the single word "Construisons" is 272px wide, but the box's content area at 320px is only 222px (x 49→271). The word runs from x 49 to 321: it crosses the box's right border (x 296) and the section's overflow-hidden cuts off the final "s" at the 320px edge. At 360 FR it still overruns the content area by 10px (right 321 vs 311), ending 14px from the border, so the right padding is lost. EN ("Let's build", 205px) fits. 320 CSS px is the width of an iPhone SE, or any iPhone with Display Zoom on.
suggested_fix: Give phones a lower minimum: `text-[clamp(2.3rem,11.5vw,3rem)] md:text-[clamp(3rem,8.2vw,8.6rem)]`. That gives "Construisons" ≈208px at 320 and ≈235px at 360, both of which fit. Add `hyphens-auto` as a safety net (the html lang is fr-CA), and optionally use px-5 instead of px-6 on the chip box below 360px.

description: The pill buttons stay stuck in their hover state on touch. `.btn:hover` isn't gated by `(hover: hover)`, so tapping LinkedIn or GitHub (which open a new tab) leaves the button inverted when you come back: paper fill, ink text, ::before at translateY(0). It looks selected or active until you tap somewhere else. Measured after a tap at 390: color rgb(11,12,14), border rgb(237,235,230), :hover=true. Download CV behaves the same way.
suggested_fix: Wrap `.btn:hover` and `.btn:hover::before` in `@media (hover: hover) { … }` and keep the `:focus-visible` variants outside it. For immediate touch feedback, add a short `.btn:active` style, such as a slight darkening or `scale(0.98)`. The same applies to `.link-underline:hover` (globals.css:360), which leaves the email underlined after a tap.

description: On touch, nothing shows the email is a link. The underline only appears on :hover or :focus-visible, and the address uses the same paper colour as the body text. On a phone it reads as plain text in an 18px box 30.6px tall, and the only thing that looks tappable nearby is the small Copy pill. Users either miss that they can tap it to write an email or tap it by accident when aiming for Copy.
suggested_fix: On devices without hover, show the underline at rest, e.g. `@media (hover: none) { #contact .link-underline { background-size: 100% 1px } }`, or add a small ↗/✉ glyph. Pad the link vertically (`py-2 -my-2`) so its hit area reaches 44px.
note: underline shown at rest on hover:none

description: The Copy pill changes width when tapped. EN grows from 60px to 94px ("COPIED ✓", +57%) and FR from 77px to 86px, then shrinks back after 1.8s. On ≥768 and in 844×390 landscape it sits inline after the email, so you can see it grow to the right under your finger. It's a small jump, but it's the only feedback the tap gives.
suggested_fix: Reserve the width by stacking both labels in one grid cell (`grid` on the button, both spans `col-start-1 row-start-1`, idle or done label `invisible`), or give it `min-w-[7.5rem] justify-center`.

viewport: real iPhone over plain-http LAN / iOS < 13.4 (not reproducible in desktop engines)
description: This concerns the Copy fallback in the working tree, which runs when navigator.clipboard is missing. It uses `field.select()` on a readonly textarea but doesn't call `setSelectionRange(0, len)`. It also leaves the textarea at its default font size (<16px), with no top/left. iOS Safari doesn't select text from `select()` alone, so `execCommand('copy')` can still return true and show "Copied ✓" even though nothing was copied. Focusing a field smaller than 16px can also trigger iOS auto-zoom. If everything fails, the address is selected with no message, which on iOS shows no callout. The desktop simulations pass: Chromium and WebKit with navigator.clipboard removed both show "COPIED ✓", with scrollY unchanged and scale 1. Real iOS is the unverified case, and it's the owner's own LAN test path.
suggested_fix: In fallback(), set `field.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;top:0;left:0;opacity:0;pointer-events:none;font-size:16px'`, then call `field.focus({preventScroll:true}); field.select(); field.setSelectionRange(0, field.value.length)`. On failure, switch the pill to a visible hint (e.g. "Hold to copy") rather than only selecting the address.

description: In landscape the space above and below the contact box is desktop-sized. With md:py-48 (192px) on contact plus the skills section's bottom padding, there's 368px of empty board between the last skill chip and the contact box, and 192px between the box and the footer. With a 390px-tall viewport and the 80px fixed header, you scroll through more than a full screen of bare traces before the box, and the box itself (612px) is 1.6 screens tall. Pages in landscape feel broken or empty.
suggested_fix: Use the existing `short:` custom variant (max-height:500px): `short:py-16` on the section, and `short:py-10` plus a smaller heading clamp on the chip box. Board.tsx re-measures on resize, so the board follows automatically.

viewport: 768 (touch tablet) and 844l landscape; EN and FR
description: At md the rows switch to a 12-column grid with md:gap-8, which spends 11×32=352px on gutters. At 768 the three columns come out at only 153, 214 and 276px (170, 238 and 305px at 844 landscape). The md:text-3xl (30px) org names wrap in 4 of 6 rows: "Independent / Tutoring", "Saint Joseph / University", "McGill / University", "Collège Mariste / Champville" (FR: "Tutorat / indépendant", "Université / Saint-Joseph", …). Roles wrap too ("Tuteur en mathématiques / Montréal"), and the description sits in a narrow ~276px column. Every row becomes a ragged 3-column block, and the one-column phone layout would read better.
suggested_fix: Keep the stacked layout until lg (`lg:grid-cols-12 lg:gap-8`), or at md use a tighter template: `md:grid-cols-[9.5rem_1fr_1.25fr] md:gap-x-8` with `md:text-2xl lg:text-3xl` on .xp-org.

description: When the FR date wraps, its two lines collide. In the 153px dates column at 768, "JUIL. — SEPT. 2026" wraps to "JUIL. — SEPT." / "2026". label-mono sets line-height:1, so the two 11.5px uppercase lines have no leading at all (box h≈23px for 2 lines), and they read as a smudge in copper next to the 30px org name. The same zero-leading wrap affects any label-mono text that wraps on tablets.
suggested_fix: Add `whitespace-nowrap` to .xp-dates, together with a column wide enough for the longest FR date (~9.5rem). Or give .xp-dates `leading-[1.45]`. More broadly, raise label-mono's line-height to about 1.3; its single-line uses won't change visually.
note: stacked until lg + leading-[1.45] on dates

description: The gap between the end of Experience and the Skills marquee is a whole screen of nothing in landscape. Experience's md:py-48 bottom (192px) plus Skills' md:py-44 top (176px) is 368px, against a 390px viewport of which the fixed header takes 80px. Mid-scroll the screen shows only the rail and the header (see screenshot). At 375 portrait the same gap is 256px, 38% of a 667px screen.
suggested_fix: Add `short:py-16` to both sections (the variant is already defined in globals.css:6 for max-height:500px), and trim phone padding to py-24 so section breaks stay under ~⅓ of the viewport.

description: The row dates (and the WORK/EDUCATION group labels and counts) are label-mono: 0.72rem = 11.52px, uppercase, 0.14em tracking. Until the trace powers a row they're also mute (#8a8f98, 6.0:1). On a phone held at arm's length, 11.5px spaced caps are at the edge of comfortable reading. Dates are real content here, unlike the decorative kicker labels.
suggested_fix: Bump label-mono to about 0.78rem (12.5px) below md, or give just .xp-dates `text-[0.8rem]` on mobile.
note: label-mono is the site-wide system size (11.5px, 6:1 contrast); changing it is a design-system decision — revisit in pass 2 consistency

description: Landscape spacing inside Skills is out of proportion to the screen. There's 163px between the marquee's bottom border and the SKILLS heading, and after the last chip the section still has md:py-44 (176px) before the contact padding starts, which gives the 368px bare stretch before the contact box. Once you add the 368px gap before the marquee (see the experience finding), Skills in 844×390 is mostly empty scrolling around a single band.
suggested_fix: Add `short:py-14` on the section and `short:mt-12` on the inner gutter (currently mt-24 md:mt-32).

description: The chips' pin pseudo-elements (5px each side, at -6px) aren't accounted for in the layout, so a chip that ends at its row's edge pushes its pins out of the column. At 390 EN the "Codex" chip's right pins reach x=372, 6px past the column/gutter edge (366). At 768 FR "Structures de données" is exactly as wide as its 208px column (x 280→488), so both pin sets stick out into the gaps. One more character in a translation would overflow the column. The chip wraps its own text rather than the row, so the pins then sit on a two-line chip.
suggested_fix: Pad the list horizontally by the pin width (`px-[6px]` on the ul), or keep the gap-x as-is and add `mx-[6px]` to each chip, so the pins stay inside the column. Add `whitespace-nowrap` on .chip so long labels move to a new row instead of breaking.
note: decorative 5px pins entering the gutter by 6px; shifting the chips would misalign them with their titles

description: The long FR labels wrap unevenly in the footer's 4-column grid. At md each column is only 161.6px (768) or 179px (844). "© 2026 GREGORY SUTJIAN" wraps to 2 lines in both locales. FR "HEURE LOCALE" wraps as "HEURE / LOCALE" with the clock to its right, while "FAIT À MONTRÉAL" and "HAUT DE PAGE ↑" stay on one line. label-mono's line-height:1 makes the wrapped lines touch (23px box for 2 lines of 11.5px). The row ends up as four items at three different heights.
suggested_fix: Use `md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4` (a 2×2 grid on tablets and landscape phones), or `md:flex md:flex-wrap md:justify-between md:gap-x-10` with `whitespace-nowrap` on each item. Wrapped footer text also needs a line-height of about 1.4.

description: All of the footer's real content is 11.52px uppercase mono with 0.14em tracking: ©, Made in Montreal, the local-time label and Back to top. Three of the four items are mute #8a8f98 (6.0:1). On a phone this is the smallest text on the page, stacked in four rows with 20px gaps, and it's also where users land at the end of the page. The FR labels are the longest ("HEURE LOCALE 17:28:08" spans ~180px of 11.5px caps).
suggested_fix: Use 0.78–0.8rem for the footer items below md (e.g. `max-md:text-[0.8rem]`), or raise label-mono's size on mobile across the page.

description: In-page nav links (desktop nav, mobile menu items, logo) scroll the page but never move keyboard focus to the target, so the next Tab continues from the header, and in reduced motion it sends the user back to the hero. 1440 reduced: Enter on 'Projects' scrolls to y=6640 with focus still on the header link. Tab x3 goes EXPERIENCE -> CONTACT -> EN/FR, and the 4th Tab lands on 'View projects' at scrollY 1198, back in the hero. 1440 motion: focus stays on the header link, so the next Tab is 'EXPERIENCE'. 390 reduced: menu 'Projects' -> focus returns to the MENU toggle (Nav.tsx:117), and the next Tab goes to 'View projects' at the top of the page. Fails WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (A) and makes the nav useless for keyboard users.
file_line: components/Nav.tsx:112-121 (go: preventDefault + scrollToTarget, focus not moved); lib/scroll.ts:31-43
suggested_fix: In scrollToTarget, after resolving the element, move focus to it: give each section (or its h2) tabIndex={-1}, then call el.focus({ preventScroll: true }), from Lenis's onComplete or right away in the native/reduced branch. For the mobile menu, close it, then focus the target instead of the toggle. Keep the focus ring off containers with [tabindex='-1']:focus{outline:none}.
verified_evidence: verify-top nav-enter-projects: focus=section#projects, next Tab=01 · Leads

description: Label in Name failure on the language switch. The visible text is 'EN / FR', but aria-label replaces it with 'Voir le site en français' on /en and 'View the site in English' on /fr, confirmed in the ARIA snapshot: link "Voir le site en français" / text: EN / FR. A speech-input user saying 'click FR' or 'click EN' cannot activate it. Fails WCAG 2.5.3 (A).
suggested_fix: Remove aria-label and let the name include the visible text, e.g. EN... keep 'EN / FR' as real text, then append : Voir le site en français. The computed name becomes 'EN / FR : Voir le site en français' and contains the visible label.
verified_evidence: verify-top lang-name: "EN/FR Voir le site en français" (visible text + lang=fr phrase)

description: Language of parts: the switch's name is in the other language (FR text on the en-CA page, EN text on the fr-CA page) with no lang attribute. An aria-label cannot carry a language, so screen readers read 'Voir le site en français' with the English voice and 'View the site in English' with the French voice. hrefLang is present, but it describes the target, not the label. Fails WCAG 3.1.2 (AA).
suggested_fix: Put the foreign-language phrase in real (visually hidden) text wrapped in <span lang={other}> inside the link, rather than in aria-label (combine with the 2.5.3 fix).
note: phrase moved from aria-label to an sr-only span with lang={other}

description: Opening the mobile menu with the keyboard doesn't move focus into the drawer in full-motion mode. After Enter on MENU, document.activeElement is still the 'CLOSE'/'FERMER' toggle immediately, at +60ms and at +1.2s (390 en, 375 fr). Cause: gsap.fromTo(el,{autoAlpha:0},...) sets visibility:hidden synchronously (Nav.tsx:78), so the el.querySelector('a').focus() two lines later (Nav.tsx:84) targets a link inside a visibility:hidden container and silently fails. With reduced motion (duration 0) focus correctly lands on 'About'. The intended focus management only works for some users.
suggested_fix: Set visibility before focusing: gsap.set(el,{display:'flex',visibility:'visible',opacity:0}); gsap.to(el,{opacity:1,...}); then focus the first link. Or focus inside the tween's onStart, or in requestAnimationFrame after the first render.

description: Escape closes the mobile menu but drops focus to <body>. With focus on a menu link, pressing Escape leaves activeElement=body after 800ms, because the drawer goes display:none and the toggle is not refocused. The next Tab restarts from the top of the document ('View projects'), not from the Menu button. Fails WCAG 2.4.3 (A) focus return. Only the link-click path (go) returns focus to the toggle.
suggested_fix: const onKey = (e) => { if (e.key === 'Escape') { setOpen(false); toggle.current?.focus(); } }. Do the same whenever the menu closes while focus is inside #mobile-menu (e.g. the resize-to-md close at Nav.tsx:89-90).

description: The focus ring on mobile menu links is clipped. Each <li> is overflow-hidden (it masks the rise-in animation), and it cuts off the 2px copper outline (offset 4px) on the top, left and right. Measured: a=[24,512,366,560], li=[24,512,366,573], outline extent 6px, so top/left/right are clipped and only the bottom edge shows, as a thin copper line that looks like the li's own border-b. WCAG 2.4.7 (AA) indicator badly degraded (2.4.13 fails).
suggested_fix:
Move the mask off the focusable element:
  • ...
    • , animating the inner span. Or give .menu-item:focus-visible an inset treatment (outline-offset:-2px, or a copper text/bar colour change).

description: With the menu open, main and footer are now inert, but the skip link is not. Tab past the last item ('Contact') leaves the page and wraps to 'Skip to content', which appears over the drawer. Its target #main is inert, so activating it does nothing while the page stays locked. Tab sequence: About, Projects, Experience, Contact, body, SKIP TO CONTENT, Logo, EN/FR, CLOSE.
suggested_fix: Add document.querySelector('.skip-link') to the `behind` list, or keep focus cycling between the header controls and the menu links while open.
note: skip link inert while menu open

description: The menu toggle changes its accessible name ('Menu' -> 'Close' / 'Fermer') and also flips aria-expanded, so screen readers announce 'Close, button, expanded', a double state signal. The disclosure pattern recommends a stable name plus aria-expanded.
suggested_fix: Keep the visible 'Menu'/'Close' swap but give the button a stable accessible name (aria-label="Menu"), or keep the text swap and drop reliance on aria-expanded wording. Don't do both.
note: visible Menu/Close swap + aria-expanded is the common disclosure pattern; a stable aria-label would break label-in-name for the Close state

description: The current language is shown by colour alone: active 'EN' is paper and inactive 'FR' is mute, a 2.73:1 difference, below the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.1 asks for when colour is the only cue. The separator '/' is #2a2d33 on ink at 1.42:1. There is no aria-current or text alternative. The page content makes the language obvious, hence P3.
suggested_fix: Add a non-colour cue to the active code (underline or font-weight) and raise the separator to text-mute. Say which language is current in the sr-only text.
note: current language is also conveyed by the sr-only phrase in the other language; colour is a secondary cue

description: During the ~2.8s boot overlay, keyboard focus goes behind the opaque overlay, and the page is left scrolled mid-way. Tab presses at t=700ms: 'Skip to content', then '01 · Leads', '02 · Designs', '03 · Demo', all covered by div.boot-half--bottom (elementFromPoint). Focusing them scrolls the locked page, and when the boot ends scrollY=8238 (Projects), so the user never sees the hero and starts mid-page. Fails WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (AA) and 2.4.3.
suggested_fix: While booting, set inert on header, #main and footer (remove it in onComplete). Or skip the intro on the first keydown/pointerdown: window.addEventListener('keydown', () => tl.progress(1), { once: true }). Also re-run window.scrollTo(0,0) in onComplete if focus hasn't moved.
verified_evidence: verify-top boot-tab-700ms: Tab skips the intro, booted=true, page inert during boot

description: The custom cursor hides the OS pointer for everyone with a fine pointer, with no opt-out. html.has-cursor *{cursor:none!important} removes the user's enlarged or high-contrast system pointer and replaces it with a 6px paper dot plus a ring that lags by 0.45s. The dot is 1.19:1 against white surfaces and the ring (paper at 35%) is 2.84:1 on ink. With forced-colors active, the cursor still activates (QUERY ignores forced-colors): the dot keeps background rgb(255,255,255) on the white Canvas, and the ring is forced to black, so it vanishes over black text. The real pointer is effectively lost.
suggested_fix: Extend QUERY with 'and (forced-colors: none) and (prefers-contrast: no-preference)'. Better: don't set cursor:none; draw the ring as an addition to the native pointer, so the OS pointer and its accessibility settings always survive.
note: custom cursor disabled with forced-colors or prefers-contrast

description: The header is visibility:hidden for 0.9s+ after load (data-intro, then autoAlpha 0 -> 1 with delay 0.9 and duration 1.4), and until ~2.9s on a first visit. Header links are out of the tab order and the accessibility tree during that time. A Tab 150ms after load gives 'Skip to content' -> 'View projects' -> 'Download CV', skipping the whole header, and VoiceOver's auto-read on load starts without the banner.
suggested_fix: Fade the header with opacity only (gsap.fromTo(el,{opacity:0,y:-16},{opacity:1,...})) and exclude header from the visibility:hidden [data-intro] rule, so it stays focusable while it fades in.
verified_evidence: verify-top tab2-at-150ms = logo link (header fades with opacity only)

description: Decorative loops run forever with no on-page pause: the grain shifts every 0.18s (steps(5) over 0.9s, infinite), plus the status-dot ping (2s infinite) and the hero hint-wire spark (2.2s infinite). They stop only when the OS reduce-motion setting is on or the device has no hover (grain). WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (A) applies to auto-starting motion that lasts over 5s beside other content. These are decorative, so P3, but a distraction for users with attention or vestibular sensitivities who haven't set the OS flag.
suggested_fix: Stop the loops after a few cycles (animation-iteration-count: 3 for ping and wire), and pause the grain when the page isn't scrolling, or drop the grain animation (a static grain looks nearly identical at 6% opacity).
note: grain/ping/wire are tiny decorative loops, all stopped by prefers-reduced-motion (and grain on touch)

description: Pass-1 skip link: after Enter on 'Skip to content', document.activeElement is <body> (the #main target had no tabindex). Chrome still moves the sequential start point (the next Tab is 'View projects'), but Safari/VoiceOver and older AT don't reliably follow a non-focusable target. NOTE: the uncommitted page.tsx adds tabIndex={-1} to <main>. Verify it after commit.
suggested_fix: Keep <main id="main" tabIndex={-1}> with #main:focus{outline:none}. Under Lenis, make sure the anchors handler doesn't preventDefault the fragment navigation; if it does, focus #main manually.
note: #main tabIndex=-1 (skip link + back to top target)

description: The 'View projects' CTA scrolls to #projects but doesn't move focus. Reduced 1440: after Enter, scrollY=6640 with focus still on the CTA, and the next Tab lands on 'Download CV' and throws the page back to scrollY 1198 (the hero). Motion 1440: after Enter, the scroll timeline sets .hero-hud-scroll to autoAlpha 0, so the focused CTA becomes visibility:hidden and focus drops to <body> (activeElement=body). Fails WCAG 2.4.3 (A).
suggested_fix: Same fix as the nav: scrollToTarget should focus the target (#projects with tabIndex={-1}, or its h2) with preventScroll once the scroll starts or finishes. Hide the hero HUD with opacity only (not autoAlpha) so it doesn't take the focused element away mid-interaction.

description: Reflow/zoom: on short viewports the hero's text overlaps. 320x256: the 'View projects' button covers 'SUTJIAN' (82x59px overlap), and the header's Logo, EN/FR and MENU sit on top of the eyebrow (overlaps 24x24, 55x12, 34x35). 480x300: both CTAs overlap name line 2 (36x16, 124x16) and the status overlaps it too (116x8). 640x310: 'Download CV' overlaps the name (26x14). Cause: the sticky frame is h-svh overflow-hidden, and the name block is flex-1 min-h-0 while the h1's minimum font is 3.4rem, so the name spills into the bottom row. Fails WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow (AA).
suggested_fix: Under the short variant, let the frame grow (min-h-svh instead of h-svh, and no overflow-hidden in reduced motion), or lower the h1 minimum (e.g. clamp(2.2rem, …) with short:) and add pt equal to the header height (4rem) so the eyebrow always clears the fixed header.
note: 400% zoom reflow of the hero: needs a short-screen layout rework (pass 2)

description: The tagline ('I like building things, from AI agents to full websites…') is display:none on every viewport 500px tall or less. That covers landscape phones and desktop users zoomed to 200% on a 1440x900 screen (720x450), who lose the only descriptive sentence in the hero, for sighted and screen-reader users alike (display:none). Content loss on zoom fails WCAG 1.4.4/1.4.10 (AA).
suggested_fix: Don't hide it. In the short variant render it at a smaller size or with line-clamp, or move it below the name block and let the hero frame grow (see the reflow fix).
note: tagline hidden at heights <=500px; pass 2 with the reflow rework

viewport: 375, 1440 (reduced motion; also motion before the intro completes)
description: Text spacing (WCAG 1.4.12, AA): with the standard overrides (letter-spacing .12em, word-spacing .16em, line-height 1.5), the name is clipped. At 375, 'Gregory' has scrollWidth 382 vs clientWidth 327 and renders 'GREGOR', and 'Sutjian' 348 vs 327 renders 'SUTJIA'. At 1440, 'Gregory' is 1337 vs 1328. Cause: .hero-name-line keeps overflow-hidden permanently in reduced motion (it is only released in the intro's onComplete), combined with a viewport-width font size.
suggested_fix: Apply the mask only when the intro will play: add overflow-hidden from JS in the motion branch, or use a class like motion-safe:overflow-hidden. Or clip vertically only (overflow-x: visible; overflow-y: clip), which still masks the rising letters.
note: line mask only set from JS when the intro plays

description: 'Download CV' starts a file download (download attribute, 79 KB PDF) with no file type or size in its name. Users of AT, and users on metered data, aren't told it's a PDF download rather than a page. WCAG 2.4.4 best practice.
suggested_fix: Append visually hidden or visible text: 'Download CV (PDF, 79 KB)', localized ('(PDF, 79 Ko)').

description: Once the hero has scrolled about 15% of its length, the timeline sets the CTAs and eyebrow to visibility:hidden (autoAlpha 0), so they drop out of the tab order. Shift+Tab from the first Projects tab jumps straight to EN/FR in the header ('01 · LEADS' -> 'EN / FR'), and the hero's CV download can only be reached at scroll top. In reduced motion the sequence includes them ('01 · LEADS' -> 'DOWNLOAD CV' -> 'VIEW PROJECTS').
suggested_fix: Tween opacity instead of autoAlpha for .hero-hud-scroll/.hero-eyebrow, and on focusin inside #top scroll the hero back to its start (scrollToTarget(0)) so a focused CTA is always visible.

description: Reduced-motion users get a 'dead scroll'. The hero section stays h-[170vh] / md:h-[190vh] with a sticky frame that nothing animates, so for 70-90vh of scrolling nothing on screen moves, which looks like a frozen page or a broken wheel. This is the static version, yet it keeps the height the scroll animation needed.
suggested_fix: Under prefers-reduced-motion use motion-reduce:h-auto on the section and a non-sticky min-h-svh frame.

description:
In full-motion mode, screen readers get nothing from the statement. SplitText's default aria:'auto' puts aria-hidden on all 31 (EN) / 41 (FR) word elements and moves the text into aria-label on the

, and aria-label is prohibited on role=paragraph (axe aria-prohibited-attr, serious; axe was only run in reduced mode in the pass-1 audit, so this was missed). The Chrome AX tree has 0 non-ignored text nodes for the sentence, and the ARIA snapshot shows 'paragraph: - emphasis' with no text. NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver generally ignore aria-label on

, so the page's key sentence is silent. The emphasis is lost too. Reduced motion is unaffected. Fails WCAG 1.3.1 / 4.1.2 (A).
suggested_fix:
Pass aria:'hidden' and add a screen-reader copy:

next to an aria-hidden visual

. Alternatively pass aria:'none' so the word spans stay readable (some screen readers then pause per word, so the sr-only copy is preferred). Add axe runs in motion mode to the audit.
verified_evidence: verify-top statement-aria: paragraph text exposed (SplitText aria:none)

description: Unlit words sit at opacity 0.13, which is 1.34:1 against ink (paper #edebe6 at 13% over #0b0c0e). The large-text minimum of 3:1 needs opacity 0.37 or more (0.40 gives 3.37:1). The words light in reading order across the scrub (start 'top 45%', end 'bottom 105%'), so most of the 120vh pin shows the tail of the sentence below 3:1. The full sentence is readable at once only in the last ~5vh of the pin, and scrolling back up dims text the user has already read. Fails WCAG 1.4.3 (AA) for the dimmed state.
suggested_fix: Raise the floor to opacity 0.4 (3.37:1) and end the scrub earlier (e.g. end: 'bottom 150%') so the sentence stays fully lit for a real dwell before the pin releases.
note: dim state is transient and scroll-controlled; raised 0.13→0.2 and the sentence now rests fully lit before the pin ends (end bottom 130%)

description: The region label is duplicated and hard-coded. The <section> has aria-label 'In one sentence' / 'En une phrase', and the first child is a visible paragraph with the same text, so screen readers announce 'In one sentence, region' followed by 'In one sentence'. The strings also live in the component instead of content/site.ts (they will drift from translations).
suggested_fix:
Give the label

an id and use aria-labelledby on the section (or drop the region naming), and move both strings to content/site.ts.

description: At 400% zoom the pinned sentence doesn't fit its frame. The sticky frame is h-svh (256px) with justify-center, and the content is 337px tall, so about 40px overflows above and below. While pinned, the first line ('My favourite part') and the label sit above the viewport and can't be scrolled into view. The screenshot starts at 'of building'. The text can only be read in pieces while it enters and leaves. WCAG 1.4.10.
suggested_fix: Use justify-content: safe center (Tailwind justify-center-safe) plus min-h-svh instead of h-svh, or drop the sticky pin under short heights / reduced motion.

description: In reduced motion the section keeps h-[220vh] with a static sticky frame, so about 120vh of scrolling moves nothing. Together with the hero's 70-90vh, reduced-motion users scroll roughly two screens with no visible change.
suggested_fix: motion-reduce:h-auto on the section and motion-reduce:static / min-h-[60svh] on the frame.

viewport: landscape phones under 768 wide: 568x320, 667x375 (iPhone SE), 740x360 (Android); also after rotating 390x844 to 667x375 with the menu open
description: The mobile menu drawer is taller than a landscape phone screen, and its first item slides under the fixed header. The drawer is `fixed inset-0 flex-col justify-end pb-16` with four 48px items (text-5xl) and no overflow handling, so the list grows upward from the bottom. Measured first item ('About'/'À propos') top/bottom: 740x360 at 28/76, 667x375 at 43/91, 568x320 at -12/36. The header strip ends at 64. At 740x360 'À propos' is drawn right through the 'GREGORY SUTJIAN' logo label. Worse, taps on it hit the header: elementFromPoint in the top 30-50% of the item returns the header's logo link, and a real touch tap there closed the menu and scrolled to the TOP (scrollY 0) instead of going to About. At 568x320 the item is entirely under the header: the tap lands on the header's gutter div and nothing happens, so About can't be reached from the menu. The header gradient also dims the item. The nav has overflow-y: visible and scrollHeight equals clientHeight, so the hidden part can't be scrolled to either.
file_line: components/Nav.tsx:179 (drawer classes: justify-end pb-16, no top padding or overflow), components/Nav.tsx:188 (text-5xl labels)
suggested_fix: Give the drawer a top inset that clears the header (pt-20), make it scrollable (overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain), and replace justify-end with mt-auto on the <ul>. An overflowing justify-end column spills past the top edge, where it can't be scrolled to; mt-auto keeps the list at the bottom when it fits. Add a short: variant for max-height 500px: short:text-3xl on the labels, short:gap-0, short:pb-6.
verified_evidence: verify-top menu-landscape-667: first item 107 > header 56; shots/nav/p1-fix/667x375-fr-menu.png

viewport: 844x390 FR (landscape phone), also 932x430 FR and 740x360 FR; motion and reduced motion
description: In landscape the pinned sentence is taller than the h-svh sticky frame, so it gets clipped at both ends for the whole 220vh pin. The font is clamp(2rem,5.4vw,5.6rem), which scales with width only: 45.6px at 844 wide gives 7 lines, 333px of text plus the label. At 844x390 FR the 'EN UNE PHRASE' label sits at top -1 (cut off at the screen edge) and the text bottom is 391 (> 390 viewport), so the descenders of 'pas encore essayé.' are cut. At 932x430 FR: label top 2, text bottom 428 of 430. At 740x360 FR: label 13, bottom 347. The reduced-motion layout clips the same way (label -1 / bottom 391).
file_line: components/Statement.tsx:50 (text-[clamp(2rem,5.4vw,5.6rem)]), components/Statement.tsx:43 (sticky h-svh justify-center), components/Statement.tsx:44 (mb-8 md:mb-12 label gap)
suggested_fix: Cap the size by height too: text-[clamp(1.6rem,min(5.4vw,8.5svh),5.6rem)], or add short:text-[min(5.4vw,8svh)]. Drop the label gap on short screens (short:mb-4). Reserve the header height at the top of the frame (pt-16 md:pt-20, or short:pt-14) so the sentence never centres under the header.

viewport: 844x390 and 932x430 (landscape phones at least 768 wide, so the desktop nav shows)
description: The header height is chosen by width only (h-16, md:h-20), so a landscape phone gets the 80px desktop header: 21% of a 390px-tall screen (measured headerBottom 80, vh 390). Scrolling up reveals it, with the new solid backdrop, over the pinned Statement. At 844x390 FR it hides the 'EN UNE PHRASE' label and the whole first line 'Mon moment préféré quand je' (text top 58 < header bottom 80). The same happens at 932x430. Over About and Projects it covers the section heading (header-over-content shot at 844l). Besides the logo, the four nav links and EN/FR, nothing in this 80px strip needs the space.
suggested_fix: Add a height-based override so short screens keep a compact bar: short:h-12, or at least short:h-14. The short custom variant (max-height 500px) already exists in globals.css. Pair this with the Statement top padding fix so pinned text centres below the bar.

viewport: all (tested 390x844 touch); first visit in a tab
description: On a first visit, deep links to a section are thrown away. Boot sets history.scrollRestoration = 'manual' and calls window.scrollTo(0,0) before the intro, and never goes back to location.hash. Opening /en#contact or /fr#projects in a fresh tab (exactly what someone tapping a shared link in LinkedIn or Messages does) ends at scrollY 0 with the hash still in the URL: #projects is 7972px below. With gs-booted already set, the same URL lands correctly (contact top 0). So a shared section link only works for people who have already visited in that tab.
file_line: components/Boot.tsx:23-24 (scrollRestoration manual + scrollTo(0,0)), components/Boot.tsx:28-35 (onComplete never restores the hash)
suggested_fix: Skip the boot when location.hash names an element: add the booted class in the head bootScript when location.hash is set, the same way it does for reduced motion. Or in Boot's onComplete, call scrollToTarget(location.hash) when one exists.
verified_evidence: verify-top deeplink-contact: contactTop 0 on a first visit

description: On phones there is about half a screen of blank scroll between the hero and the Statement. Scroll samples at 375x667: the name's opacity reaches 0.015 at scrollY 334 and hero-fade is at 1 by 500. The Statement label only enters the viewport around scrollY 620-700 (label top 684 at 611, 572 at 723), and the first word lights at 889. From about y 334 to 690 (around 360px, 55% of the viewport) the screen is just the dark background and the copper trace; to 889 the sentence is only at 13% opacity. A normal thumb flick lands inside this gap, and the page looks like it stopped loading. The hero is 170vh, so only 70vh drives the gate, and the gate is done by 0.4-0.75 of it.
file_line: components/hero/Hero.tsx:96-105 (name out by 0.4-0.72, hero-fade at 0.85), components/hero/Hero.tsx:154 (h-[170vh]), components/Statement.tsx:30 (start 'top 45%')
suggested_fix: Close the gap on small screens. Either pull the Statement up under the hero's last frame on phones (a negative margin-top of about 40svh on the Statement section, since the hero frame is ink by then), or shorten the hero's fade-out so it overlaps the Statement's entry (h-[150vh] on phones and hero-fade at 0.95). Starting the Statement's lighting at 'top 70%' would also show the text sooner.
note: phone gap between hero gate and statement; pass 2

description: The sentence finishes lighting only 5vh before the pin lets go, so on a phone it never rests fully lit. The tween ends at 'bottom 105%' and the pin ends at 'bottom 100%'. At 375x667 the last word lights at scrollY of about 1901 and the text starts scrolling away at about 1934, just 33px later. The last line ('whatever I haven't tried yet' / 'pas encore essayé') is only fully readable while it is already leaving.
suggested_fix: End the lighting earlier so the fully lit sentence holds for part of the pin, e.g. end: 'bottom 135%' (about 35vh of rest).

viewport: iOS Safari phones (not reproducible in Chromium; reasoned from CSS)
description: Sticky frames are h-svh inside sections sized in vh (170vh, 220vh). Once Safari's toolbar collapses, which happens on the first scroll and so for the whole gate, the visual viewport grows to lvh. The hero frame then stops about 80-100px above the bottom of the screen. The grid floor and glow end in a hard line at the svh edge (the floor mask is still 30% opaque at the bottom), and the bottom HUD row no longer sits at the bottom. The Statement frame's vertical centre shifts the same way.
file_line: components/hero/Hero.tsx:155 (sticky top-0 h-svh), components/Statement.tsx:43 (sticky top-0 h-svh)

description: Both hero CTAs ('View projects' / 'Voir les projets', 'Download CV' / 'Télécharger le CV') are 43px tall, just under the 44px minimum. btn-sm padding of 0.8rem plus the 0.66rem mono line comes to 43px. These are the main actions on the first screen.

description: In the short landscape layout the name almost touches the CTA row. description: Opening the menu changes the toggle's label from 'Menu' (34px wide) to 'Fermer' (51px) or 'Close' (43px). The right-aligned row reflows, and the EN/FR switch next to the thumb jumps left: by 17px in FR (from x 257 to 240 at 390) and 8px in EN. description: The only way to close the drawer is the small 'Close' text at the far top-right (x of about 323-366, y 12-52 at 390x844), the hardest spot to reach one-handed on a tall phone. The drawer is full screen and its upper 60% is empty (the items start at y 512 of 844), but tapping that empty area does nothing, and there is no swipe-down to close either.

description: On short and common laptop windows the giant name runs into the bottom row. 'SUTJIAN' overlaps the tagline and the SCROLL hint. Measured at 1280x620: line-2 glyph box bottom is 505 while the tagline top is 458 (EN) or 429 (FR). The tagline's right edge is 481 and SUTJIAN starts at x=389, so they overlap by 92px horizontally and 47-76px vertically, and the SCROLL label top (500) sits under the letters. The same collision shows at 1366x650 (bottom 531 vs tagline 488/459), 1440x700 (566 vs 538), 1536x730 (594 vs 568) and 1024x640 (482 vs 449). In FR, where the tagline has 3 lines, it also happens at 1280x720 (555 vs 529), 1366x768 (590 vs 577, the most common laptop screen) and 1440x760 (596 vs 569, where 'aux' ends 3px from the S). On md+ the name size depends only on width (16.4vw) and is centered in the whole frame (roomy:absolute inset-0), with no account of how tall the bottom row is.
file_line: components/hero/Hero.tsx:201 (md:text-[clamp(3.4rem,16.4vw,17.5rem)] has no height term); components/hero/Hero.tsx:189 (roomy:absolute roomy:inset-0 centers the name over the full frame); app/globals.css:4 (roomy = min-height 501px, so 620-800px-tall windows get the full-screen layout)
suggested_fix: Add a height cap on md+, e.g. md:text-[clamp(3.4rem,min(16.4vw,25svh),17.5rem)]. Or drop the absolute centering and use a flex column (name flex-1 centered, bottom row in normal flow) so the name can never extend into the HUD. Raising the roomy min-height (e.g. to 820px) also works.

description: The group of nav links is not centered on the page. justify-between with a wide left block (Mark + name, 163px) and a narrow right block (EN/FR, 54px) pushes the group 54.6px right of center at every width: its center is at 774.6 vs 720 at 1440, 1014.6 vs 960 at 1920, 438.6 vs 384 at 768, and 476.6 vs 422 at 844l. The hero puts its SCROLL label, the wire and the copper start pad exactly on the page's center line, right below the nav, so two 'centered' elements visibly disagree by about 55px.

description: In the boot overlay the logo and name sit right on the glowing copper bar instead of above it. The class translate-y-[-3.25rem] is meant to hold the mark 52px above the line, but GSAP takes over the CSS translate and tweens y to 0. Measured at the end: computed translate 'none', transform identity, mark top 450 equals bar y 450. The mark slides down into the line on entry, and the bar's 18px glow bleeds over the icon and the 'GREGORY SUTJIAN' label, so the one-time intro looks crowded.
suggested_fix: Put the offset on the layout instead of a transform, e.g. top-[calc(50%-3.25rem)] or a wrapper div, then animate the inner mark with fromTo({y:8},{y:0}). Or tween to y:-52 explicitly.
note: offset via top calc, rise-in fromTo y:8

description: In French the two hero CTAs don't fit on one row. 'VOIR LES PROJETS' and 'TÉLÉCHARGER LE CV' stack into two pills of different widths (179px vs 170px at 390; 179 vs 169 at 768; tops 885 and 941 at 768). The FR tagline also grows to 4 lines, so the left block is about 230px tall against a one-line status on the right. The row looks lopsided and different from EN, where both CTAs sit side by side.

note: lg: text column 1.5fr + hint centred absolutely (FR CTAs one row at ≥1024); at 768 the 3-col layout stays (CTAs wrap)

description: The type hierarchy is inverted in the bottom row. The primary CTAs use .btn-sm at 0.66rem (10.56px), which makes them the smallest text in the hero. They are smaller than the passive mono labels: eyebrow, status and nav at 0.72rem (11.52px), and the SCROLL hint. At 1920 'VIEW PROJECTS' reads weaker than 'OPEN TO INTERNSHIPS' next to it.

description: The share card is missing its intended glow and edge fade. The overlay meant to 'soften the grid toward the edges + copper horizon glow' does not render. The pixel at the glow center (840,378) is exactly ink #0b0c0e, and grid lines are exactly #2a2d33 at the corners and in the center. suggested_fix: Satori doesn't render that 'background' shorthand with two 'ellipse at' radial gradients. Use two stacked absolute divs, each with a single backgroundImage: 'radial-gradient(circle at 70% 60%, rgba(232,130,58,0.18), transparent 55%)' and a vignette. Or bake the background into a static PNG and draw it with .

description: The share card doesn't match the site hero. It prefixes the eyebrow with a copper '[00]' index that appears nowhere in the hero (the site uses a short copper rule), and it left-aligns both name lines where the site right-aligns 'SUTJIAN'. People who click through land on a different-looking composition.
suggested_fix: Swap '[00]' for a 32x1 copper rule like the hero eyebrow, and set alignSelf:'flex-end' (or a left margin) on the last-name span to echo the hero's staggered name.
note: copper rule instead of [00], last name right-aligned

description: The display name is optically inset from the gutter on both sides, so it doesn't line up with the column around it. At 1440 the 'G' ink starts at x=66 while the eyebrow rule, tagline and nav logo start at 56-57. At 1920 it is 68 vs 57. On the right, 'SUTJIAN' ends at 1374 against 1384 for 'OPEN TO INTERNSHIPS' and EN/FR (1853 vs 1864 at 1920). At 236-280px the letters' side bearings add up to about 10-12px.

note: optical inset is under 10px and SplitText-driven; not worth the risk

description: The decorative circuit traces aren't staying in the bands they were designed for. At 1440x900 one trace runs at y≈787, right under the tagline's second line and touching the descenders of 'always up… learning', and another at y≈727 runs just above line 1. On short windows the top band slides up behind the nav: at 1280x620 a trace at y=63 with a pad at (632,63) sits under 'PROJECTS', and at 1440x760 there are pads at (710,103) and (796,78). This happens because the SVG's 'slice' crop moves the bands as the aspect ratio changes, and the top mask only fades 4-16% of the height.
suggested_fix: Position the two trace bands relative to the layout (one SVG above the name and one above the HUD) instead of one sliced full-bleed board. Or make the top mask a fixed pixel fade (transparent 0-110px) so traces never reach the nav row.

description: The status line sits a bit low next to the CTAs. 'OPEN TO INTERNSHIPS' is placed with a hard-coded md:pb-3 instead of being centered on the CTA row, so it lands about 3.5px low: text center ≈842 vs button center 838.5 at 1440, and ≈1022 vs 1018.5 at 1920.

note: md:pb-4 centres the status on the 44px CTA row

description: The pinned display sentence has a ragged right edge with dangling one-letter words. Three of six lines end on a lone 'I' ('moment I', 'works. I', 'whatever I'), which is noticeable at 78-90px. The copper italic accent ('actually' / 'vraiment') also reads smaller than the words around it, because Instrument Serif's x-height is much lower than Geist's at the same font size.
suggested_fix: Add text-wrap:pretty on the statement paragraph (and check that SplitText autoSplit keeps it), and scale .accent to about 1.1em in display contexts (e.g. .text-display .accent {font-size:1.1em; line-height:0}).

description: When focused, the skip link (fixed at 12px/12px, 160x36) lands on top of the header logo and leaves '…TJIAN' of the name sticking out to its right. It also has square corners, unlike every other control on the page (pill buttons, 3px chips).
suggested_fix: Give it an opaque bar that covers the whole logo cluster (left: var(--gutter), min-width matching the logo block, top aligned to the header row) with border-radius 999px like .btn, or offset it below the header row (top: 5.5rem).
note: skip link pill at the gutter

description: A focused nav link shows two stacked lines at the bottom. .link-underline also fires on :focus-visible, drawing a 1px underline 3px below the text, while the 2px focus outline sits 4px out. The result is an underline 1-2px inside the ring's bottom edge (ABOUT, PROJECTS, EXPERIENCE, CONTACT in tab03-06).
suggested_fix: Drop :focus-visible from the .link-underline selector (the ring is enough), or raise the outline-offset for .link-underline to 7px so the two lines separate cleanly.

description: There is a large dead band after the statement. Its text is centered in a full-height sticky frame, so after the pin releases there are about 378px of empty ink (last line ends at y=270, About label at y=648 in the 1440 shot), more than 40% of the viewport. That is noticeably looser than the rhythm between the other sections.
suggested_fix: Shorten the tail, e.g. end the section at calc(220vh - 20vh) or add a negative margin-bottom (-mb-[20svh]) to the section, so About arrives sooner once the last word lights.

description: The role / place line breaks right after the separator, leaving a dangling slash at the line end ('Tuteur en mathématiques /' then 'Montréal'; 'Concours d'entrepreneuriat /' then 'Beyrouth'; EN 'Entrepreneurship Competition' wraps the same way at 768). This happens in 4 of 6 FR rows at 768.
suggested_fix: Wrap the slash and place in a whitespace-nowrap span (`/ {place}`) so the pair moves to the next line together.

description: The rail pads don't line up with what they power. (a) The section-label pad centre is 6.2px below the copper dash it should connect to (1440: dash y=10979.2, pad centre 10985.4; same 6.2px on every viewport and in Skills). (b) Each row pad sits 12px below the row separator but 32px (375) to 40px (768-1920) above the dates line, so it lines up with neither the copper sweep line nor the text.

For .xp-row, use the row's top edge (y) so the pad sits on the separator that .xp-row::before sweeps, or the .xp-dates centre. A data-pad-offset attribute could pick the mode.
note: pads at label centre / row top edge

description: The page has no max content width. Built practice' = 100 chars), well past the ~75ch comfortable measure. The dates column is 430px wide for about 120px of text, which leaves a 340px dead gap before the org titles at x=516.

Add max-w-[62ch] to the description

, and/or change the spans at xl to 2/4/6 (dates narrower). Or cap the section content with a max-w-[1600px] wrapper.

description: On row hover, only the org <h3> shifts right by 10px (.xp-row:hover .xp-org translateX(10px)). The role/place line under it stays put, so the middle column's left edge goes ragged by 10px while hovered and the title comes loose from its subtitle.

description: When powered, every row draws a copper line on its top edge, but the last row of each group keeps its plain grey border-b. Both lists (Work, Education) end on a grey rule under a stack of copper ones, so the powered state looks unfinished at the bottom.

note: last row grey rule closes the list; P3

description: Too much dead space around the marquee. From the last Experience row to the marquee band there is 368px of empty ink at 768 and up (Experience pb-48 192px + Skills pt-44 176px), about 41% of a 900px viewport. At 375 it is 256px, 38% of a 667px screen. The same 368px sits between the last skill chip and the contact chip box, filled only by the board's top traces on wide screens and mostly empty at 375/768. The marquee band already works as a divider, so the extra padding just stacks up.

description: The copper rail (1.5px core + 7px halo) is drawn on top of the marquee words. CircuitTrace's absolute wrapper paints over the static marquee div, so a copper stripe cuts through the solid 'S' of SOFTWARE/LOGICIEL at x=28 (1440) and x=12 (375). In motion the glowing spark also slides over the letters. Everywhere else the rail stays in the gutter and never crosses text.

description: The outlined marquee words keep the solid words' tracking (-0.04em). With a 2px stroke, the outlines of neighbouring glyphs touch and merge (P-Y, Y-T, T-H, H-O in PYTHON; A-I in AI), so the outlined words read as one fused contour instead of letters. The solid words look fine.

description: With reduced motion the band doesn't move, so its crop is permanent. The first word starts at x=0 (glyph flush to the viewport edge, under the rail) while all other content sits on the 24-56px gutter, and the right side cuts mid-word ('C' at 1440, 'AGENT' at 1920).

description: md:grid-cols-3 applies at 768, giving 209px columns. Foundations stacks one chip per row (3 rows). The FR 'Structures de données' chip fills the whole column, and its right pin marks overflow 5.3px into the column gap. Languages splits 2+2 and AI 1+2+1. description: Chip rows leave orphans. At 1440, Foundations wraps 2+1 ('Mathematics' alone) and AI wraps 3+1 ('Gemini' alone) even though the Languages row fits all 4. At 375, Languages wraps 3+1 ('Bash' alone). The 20px gap-x plus 6px pin overhang on each side is what pushes the last chip down.
