note: chip wraps depend on copy length; P3

description: Two different tag styles show the same kind of content (tech names). Skills uses .chip (3px radius, graphite fill, 0.8rem mono, pin marks). The Projects 'Stack' rows use rounded-full outline pills (text-xs mono, no fill). Next to each other on the page, the tech tags look like two unrelated systems.
suggested_fix: Pick one tag language. For example, give Projects stack tags a small variant of .chip (3px radius, no pins, text-xs), or document the pill as the 'meta tag' and the chip as the 'skill' variant.
note: stack pills (meta) vs skill chips (feature) are deliberately different

description: The email row uses items-center to align an 11.5px mono label, a 33.6px email link and a 29.5px pill, so the baselines don't line up. The label and the Copy text sit 6.1px above the email's baseline at 1440/1920 (label/copy baseline 14348.9 vs email 14355.0) and 3.1px above at 1024. The small caps look like they float above the address.
suggested_fix: Use `items-baseline` on the row. Flex baseline alignment uses the pill's text baseline, so 'EMAIL', the address and 'COPY' share one baseline. Keep gap-y for the wrapped mobile layout.

description: The Copy button is a one-off button style. It is 29.5px tall, label-mono 0.72rem with 0.14em tracking, a line border, and a copper text/border colour on hover. The .btn buttons 40px below are 53.4px tall, 0.74rem with 0.12em tracking, and use a paper fill-sweep hover. The type sizes and trackings nearly match but not quite, and the hover language differs. It looks like it comes from a different kit than the pills around it.
suggested_fix: Add a .btn-xs variant in globals.css (e.g. padding 0.55rem 0.9rem, 0.66rem, same 0.12em tracking and fill-sweep) and use `btn btn-xs` for Copy, so every pill in the box shares one type size, tracking and hover.
note: Copy is an inline utility, intentionally lighter than the action buttons (and its tap-area pseudo would be clipped by .btn overflow)

description: The trace's end pad (9px square) is centred on the chip box's left edge (1440: pad x 203.5-212.5, box x 208), but the box is z-[2] above the trace's z-[1]. Only the left half of the pad shows, as a stray copper notch on the border, instead of a solder joint where the signal plugs in.
suggested_fix: Either end the route 5px short of the box (tx = c.x - 5) so the whole pad sits outside the box, or render the pads of the contact trace above the box (z-[3] on .trace-pad in #contact) so the pad sits on the border.

description: The chip-corner brackets are square 14px L-shapes with no radius, laid over a box border rounded to 6px. At each corner the square bracket and the rounded border show two different geometries, with a sliver of background between them. It is most visible when powered (copper on copper).
suggested_fix: Give each bracket the matching corner radius (rounded-tl-[6px] etc. on the four spans), or square the box (rounded-[3px] to match the skill chips, which also makes the chip metaphor consistent).

description: Board traces on the top side that run 'toEdge' end at the contact section's top boundary (y=-4) in open page space under the Skills chips (1440: traces at x≈180 and x≈1106 end mid-air, no pad). The bottom traces end on the footer's border-t, which reads as intentional, but the top ones look clipped.
suggested_fix: For side < 0 (top edge), never use toEdge: always end on a pad. Or fade the board's top 120px with a mask-image linear-gradient on the Board root.

description: The two 'Download CV' buttons don't match. The hero uses `btn btn-sm` with no glyph, and Contact uses a full-size `btn btn-primary` with a ↓ glyph. Same action, same file, different glyph treatment.
suggested_fix: Add the ↓ glyph to the hero CV button (aria-hidden), or remove it here. The size difference can stay.
note: hero CV glyph would make EN CTAs wrap at 768

description: The contact label doesn't use SectionHeader, so it drifts from the other section labels. The label-to-heading gap is 32px (mt-8) vs 24px (mt-6) elsewhere, and its copper dash lacks .section-index, so it never gets the powered glow the other labels get, even though the whole box lights up around it.
suggested_fix: Add `section-index` to the dash, add a `.contact.is-powered .section-index` glow rule, and use mt-6 on the h2 (or scale the gap in proportion to the larger heading on purpose).

description: The equal-width 4-column grid with short, left-aligned mono text leaves uneven visual gaps between the meta items (1024 FR: about 52px, 110px, 160px) and lines them up with nothing above (at 1440 the items start at 56/393/730/1067 while the contact box spans 208-1232).
suggested_fix: Use flex justify-between (equal gaps between items), or align the two middle items to the contact box's edges.

description: The giant outlined 'SUTJIAN' is cropped about 16% at the bottom on every width (1440: glyph bottom 15033.8 vs page end 15004.8, 29px of 187px; 1920: 39px of 249px; 375: 7.8px of 48.6px). That cuts the bowls of S, U and J but is too little to read as a deliberate 'sinking' crop, so it looks slightly mis-sized.
suggested_fix: Decide one way. Show the word fully (remove margin-bottom:-2.4vw, keep leading-[0.78] with a small pb), or crop it on purpose to about 35-45% (margin-bottom about -6vw).

description: The giant mark covers only about 67% of the viewport width (964/1440, 514/768, 251/375) and is centred. Its edges line up with neither the page gutter (56px) nor the contact box (208px), and at 375 the 'huge' last name is just 65px tall, smaller than the contact heading above it.
suggested_fix: Size the word to span gutter to gutter (about 24vw for 7 letters at this tracking, or fit it with a measured scale), so it reads as a full-bleed signature.

description: Resizing or rotating the window across the point where Focus switches to horizontal/pinned mode throws the reader back to the top of the page. Steps: 1100x650, scroll to #contact (y=15309), widen to 1300x650. Observed: scrollY 15309 -> 0 (hero on screen). The same happens on iPad mini rotation portrait->landscape (y 20006 -> 0), and 600->800 or 700->1440 wide at 900 tall. It never happens in the reverse direction, or on resizes that don't cross the Focus breakpoint (800->1100: position kept). Expected: stay on the contact section.
suggested_fix: When the HORIZONTAL matchMedia context is created, record the scroll anchor first (topmost visible section id + offset), then restore it after the pin and section height are applied: ScrollTrigger.addEventListener('refresh', …) once, or gsap.matchMedia's context callback followed by ScrollTrigger.refresh() and scrollTo(anchor). At minimum, save window.scrollY before size() and put it back after the pin ScrollTrigger is created.
verified_evidence: verify-c resize-threshold: projects@900 → projects@624 (same fraction), no jump to top

description: Reloading the page restores the wrong scroll position, 1000-1850px lower than where the reader was. Steps: 1440x900 in a booted session, wheel down to Experience (y=12600, Experience top -802), press reload. Observed: y=14446, Experience top -2648, so the reader lands in Skills/Contact. Also Skills y 14400 -> 15121 (bottom), 1920: 12960 -> 14336, 768: 14400 -> 15416. At 390 (Focus stays stacked) restoration is exact. The browser restores the pre-hydration offset, and Focus then grows the page (section.style.height plus the pin) above the reader.
suggested_fix: Take over restoration: on pagehide store {sectionId, offsetWithinSection} in sessionStorage, set history.scrollRestoration='manual', and after the first ScrollTrigger.refresh() (fonts.ready) scroll to that section + offset. Or reserve Focus's final height in CSS so the layout doesn't change after hydration.

description: The GitHub social button leads to a 404. https://github.com/gregorysudjian-ui returns 404 and the GitHub API reports no such user (also checked gregorysutjian-ui and gregorysutjian: 404). Note the spelling 'sudjian' vs the name 'Sutjian'. A recruiter clicking the button sees a GitHub 'Not Found' page.
suggested_fix: Put in the correct GitHub handle, or remove the GitHub button until the profile exists. Add a link check to CI.
note: OWNER ACTION: github.com/gregorysudjian-ui returns 404; the right handle is unknown, so the link is left as is and flagged in the report

description: Copy gives no feedback when copying fails. Steps: navigator.clipboard undefined (plain-http preview or older webview) and document.execCommand('copy') returns false, then press Copy. Observed: the label stays 'Copy', role=status stays empty, and the only effect is an invisible selection of the mailto link (which is off the button and easy to miss). The user thinks nothing happened. Expected: an error state such as 'Press ⌘C / Ctrl+C to copy' or 'Couldn't copy' next to the selected address, announced in the status region. (Earlier failures are fixed: the rejection is caught, the fallback works, rapid clicks keep 'Copied' visible for 1.8s after the last click, and focus returns to the button.)
suggested_fix: Add a third state, failed: show '⌘C to copy' / 'Ctrl+C pour copier' in the pill for ~3s, set the status text, and keep the selection on the address.
note: both copy APIs failing is very rare; the address is then selected as visible feedback

description: The finale switches itself off while the contact box is still on screen. Steps: scroll to the bottom (board lit, 108/108 traces) and scroll up. Observed: after ~740px of scroll-up, the section loses is-powered, all traces retract in 0.5s, pads go dark and the glow fades. At that moment the chip box is still on screen (top at y=390 of 900), heading and email visible. Anyone who scrolls up a little to re-read the heading watches the board die. The same toggle fires again on the way back down, replaying the 1.1s plus stagger animation.
suggested_fix: Latch the finale: once onPowered(true) fires, ignore false until the contact section has fully left the viewport (a separate ScrollTrigger on #contact with onLeaveBack), or never power off. Hysteresis would also do (off only below progress 0.6).
note: scroll-linked power-down is the concept; it re-powers on the way back down

viewport: 1440x900, Slow 3G-like (500kbps, 400ms RTT) + 4x CPU throttle, dev build
description: Loading is indistinguishable from nothing. Steps: booted session, throttle, open /en#contact. Observed: from about 3s to 22s the viewport shows an empty chip box (border and corners only). Heading, text, email, Copy, CV and socials are all opacity:0 because html.js [data-reveal] hides them until GSAP runs. There is no board and the clock reads '--:--:--'. At ~23s the content fades in and the page jumps from y=12733 to 14579 as Focus grows above. There is no skeleton, no timeout fallback and no minimum content. Dev bundles exaggerate the delay, but on a real phone on a weak connection the gap is still a blank box where the contact details should be.
suggested_fix: Don't pre-hide the contact essentials (email row and buttons) at all, or add a CSS failsafe: html.js [data-reveal]{animation: reveal-failsafe 0s 3s forwards} that sets opacity 1 if Reveals hasn't mounted (Reveals adds html.reveals-ready to cancel it).

description: If the JS bundles fail to load (flaky network, CDN error, content blocker, old browser that fails to parse them), Experience, Skills and Contact stay invisible forever. The inline head script has already added html.js, so every [data-reveal] element stays at opacity:0 with nothing to reveal it. Observed with /_next/static/*.js blocked: Experience shows only the top border line of the list, no rows (10/10 reveal elements at opacity 0). The contact chip is empty. On a first visit it is worse: the boot overlay (.boot stays display:block because 'booted' is never added) covers the whole page in ink. Real no-JS (JS disabled) is fine, because html.js is never set.
suggested_fix: Add a timed CSS failsafe for html.js [data-reveal] and .boot (e.g. an animation that forces opacity 1 / display none after 4s unless a class set by the React tree cancels it), or set html.js from the first client component instead of a pre-bundle inline script.
note: head-script failsafe drops html.js after 8s without the app

description: Rotating or resizing loses the reader's place, even when it doesn't jump to the top. The absolute scrollY is kept while the content above reflows. Steps (phone): at 390x844 scroll to #contact, rotate to landscape (it clamps to the bottom), rotate back to portrait. Observed: y=14757, so the reader is in Experience with contact 2902px below. Desktop: at #contact (1440x900) narrow to 1200. Observed: contact top at +2750px, Experience on screen. Rotating at Experience row 2 lands in Contact.
suggested_fix: In ScrollTrigger 'refreshInit', record the element at the top of the viewport and its offset. On 'refresh', scroll so it is back at the same offset (lenis.scrollTo(..., {immediate:true}) or window.scrollTo).

description: A repeat Copy click gets no confirmation. Steps: click Copy, click again 0.8s later. Observed: the role=status region changes once ('Email address copied') and is cleared 1.8s after the second click. The second click produces no announcement and no visible change, because the pill already says 'Copied ✓'. The user can't tell that the second click did anything.
suggested_fix: On a repeat success, clear the status text and set it again on the next frame, and give the ✓ a short pulse or re-run the label transition.

viewport: desktop resize 600->1440 (any resize or rotation that adds traces)
description: The lit board partly replays after a resize. Board regenerates on every ResizeObserver change and useGSAP re-runs the power-on tweens with the stagger. After growing from 600 to 1440, only 29/108 traces are lit at +60ms. The new traces draw in over ~1.5s and pads fade in again, so the finished board flickers into a half-built state on every window resize or phone rotation.
suggested_fix: Track whether the power-on has already played. If powered is unchanged and only geo changed, gsap.set(lit,{strokeDashoffset:0}) and set the pads' colours instantly instead of tweening with a stagger.
note: board shows lit instantly after a resize

description: Rows un-power while the reader is looking at them. is-powered is removed as soon as the trace retreats above a row's pad, which happens when the row drops below the 62% anchor line. Scrolling up a little turns the row you just read back to mute grey mid-screen, with the copper rule retracting. In the mid-section test, rows at y=827 and y=976 of 900 were unpowered while visible. Same latch question as the contact board.
suggested_fix: Latch pads/targets on (only call setPad(k,false) when progress returns to 0 or the section leaves the viewport), or move the anchor lower for the un-power direction (hysteresis).

description: Rows look clickable but aren't. Hovering an Experience row slides the organisation name 10px to the right, the usual 'this row is a link' cue, but rows have no link, no cursor change and no action. Clicking does nothing.
suggested_fix: Drop the hover nudge, or make the rows real links (e.g. to the organisation or a detail) with a visible arrow.

description: The marquee's per-frame tick keeps running after the band is paused. gsap.ticker.add(tick) is registered once and never removed while the band is off screen, so loop.timeScale() is set 60 times a second for the life of the page (the loop itself is paused, measured delta 0 when off screen). This is wasted main-thread work on phones and competes with the scroll-driven CircuitTrace renders.
suggested_fix: Add the tick in onToggle when active and remove it when inactive, alongside loop.play()/pause().

description: The clock placeholder doesn't match what replaces it under reduced motion. Server HTML and first paint show '--:--:--' (8 chars). After mount with prefers-reduced-motion the clock renders 'HH:MM' (5 chars), so the text changes format and gets ~3 characters narrower. On slow connections '--:--:--' stays up until hydration (about 20s in the throttled dev test).
suggested_fix: Use '--:--' as the placeholder when seconds are hidden (or always show HH:MM in the placeholder), and give <time> a min-width in ch so the swap never changes width.

description: The © year is computed at render in a statically generated client component. The prerendered HTML freezes the build year, so from January 1 until the next deploy the client renders a different year. That is a text hydration mismatch: React logs a recoverable error and re-renders on the client, and the year visibly changes after load.
suggested_fix: Render the year inside a suppressHydrationWarning span, or set it after mount like the clock. Alternatively, accept the build year and rebuild yearly.

description: Reading order: the Datasheet card (the 'Datasheet GS-26' text, the portrait, a 4-row <dl> and the footer) comes before the section label and the h2 'Hi, I'm Gregory.' in the DOM. Screen readers read the card first. Jumping to the About heading lands after it, so the card is out of context, and the same facts appear twice (Origin 'Lebanon → Montreal' / Based in 'Montreal'). This is a 1.3.2 meaningful-sequence and best-practice issue.
suggested_fix: Put the text column (SectionHeader + paragraphs) first in the DOM and move the datasheet column visually with md:order-first, or make the card a <figure>/<aside aria-label> so it's announced as a complementary unit after the heading.
note: text column first in DOM, card order-first

description: The Datasheet card has no accessible name or structure. Its title row is two bare spans that read as 'Datasheet GS-26' run together ('Fiche technique GS-26' in FR), so nothing tells assistive tech that the portrait and the <dl> belong to one card. 'GS-26' is read as a word or number ('G S minus 26' in some voices).
suggested_fix: Wrap the card in role="group" (or <figure>) with aria-labelledby pointing at the title span; give the part number aria-hidden or an aria-label like 'part GS 26'.
note: role=group labelled by the Datasheet title; part number aria-hidden

description: The sticky datasheet is taller than short viewports. At 1280x620 the card is 682px tall at top:112px, so its bottom sits at 794px, past the 620px viewport. While it's stuck, the Origin and Status rows and the footer can't be seen until the whole About column has scrolled past. The same happens to anyone using browser zoom or a larger default font on a laptop. This hurts low-vision and magnifier users (1.4.10-adjacent).
suggested_fix: Make it sticky only when it fits: e.g. [@media(min-width:768px)_and_(min-height:840px)]:sticky, or cap it with max-h-[calc(100svh-8rem)] and let the image shrink.
note: sticky only at lg + min-height 840px (tall variant)

description: Horizontal Focus section: bringing panel 2 or 3 into view with find-in-page, a screen reader's virtual cursor, or a magnifier's focus tracking scrolls the overflow:hidden sticky .focus-frame sideways. The page never resets that scroll, so the layout breaks for good. Measured by calling scrollIntoView() on the 'Math' h3 at the section start: frame.scrollLeft went 0 → 1846px at 1440 (1651px at 1280x620). After another 400px of wheel scroll the panels sat at x=[-2279..-1242], [-1210..-173], [-141..895]. Panels 1-2 and the section heading had left the viewport and panel 3 kept sliding off, over empty space. Paging the whole page with PageDown does work (12 presses moved the track the full -1846px), so keyboard scrolling itself is fine. The problem is programmatic scroll-into-view, which is exactly how assistive tech brings offscreen content into view.
suggested_fix: Use overflow: clip instead of hidden on .focus-frame; clip can't be scrolled by code, so it can't get out of step. Better still, listen for 'scroll' on the frame: when scrollLeft ≠ 0, map it to the matching page position (section top + scrollLeft, since the mapping is 1:1), set frame.scrollLeft = 0, then window.scrollTo(target). Find-in-page and the screen reader then land on the right panel.

viewport: 1440, 1920 (horizontal mode; text-only zoom / large default font)
description: At 200% text size (Firefox 'Zoom text only' or a large default font in Chrome, simulated with html font-size 200%, FR), the horizontal panels keep their fixed height, min(54vh,560px), and overflow-hidden, so the body text is cut off. At 1440 the panels are 325px tall and the last line sits 322/345/462px below each panel's bottom; at 1920 it is 114/137/254px below. The focus-compact fallback switches on but isn't enough, and the h3 and illustration sizes are vw/vh-based, so they don't give way. Only the heading and the first line of body text show (WCAG 1.4.4 Resize text).
file_line: app/globals.css:518-521 (.focus-panel height), components/focus/Focus.tsx:42-51 (size() tooTight check only toggles compact)
suggested_fix: When tooTight is still true after applying focus-compact, drop the horizontal layout (revert the matchMedia branch and use the stacked list), or give panels min-height instead of height. Re-run size() on a ResizeObserver of .focus-body so font-size changes are caught too, not just refreshInit.
note: 200% text-only zoom in horizontal Focus: pass 2

description: Panel 1's CodeWindow illustration is plain HTML and isn't aria-hidden, unlike the NeuralNet and MathPlot SVGs. Screen readers read it out before the 'Software' heading: 'agent.py 1 def run_agent(task): 2 context = memory.recall(task) … 8 # → done. ship it.' On /fr this is English text inside lang=fr-CA with no lang override (3.1.2 Language of parts). The line numbers are text-line #2a2d33 on ink, 1.42:1, and they are exposed to assistive tech. The decorative panel numbers '01'/'02'/'03' are also read as text before each h3 ('text: 02').
suggested_fix: Add aria-hidden="true" to the CodeWindow root div, as the two SVGs have. Add aria-hidden to the 0{i+1} span and the decorative square at Focus.tsx:131-132.

description: Endless decorative motion with no user control: all three Focus illustrations run GSAP timelines with repeat:-1 (code typing plus a blinking .caret, the network pulses, the sine readout), and the copper status-dot 'ping' loops forever in the Datasheet and on every project status pill. They loop while visible, next to text people are reading, and last well over 5s. The only way to stop them is the OS reduced-motion setting, which a page control can't replace under WCAG 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide). Rated P2 rather than P1 because it is decorative and reduced motion is honoured.
suggested_fix: Play each illustration once, or for a bounded number of loops (e.g. repeat: 2), then rest on the final frame; give the status-dot ping an animation-iteration-count of about 3. Alternatively, add one global 'Pause animations' toggle that sets a data-paused attribute the CSS and the timelines both obey.

description: Remaining problem after the opacity-only reveal fix: keyboard focus now lands on controls that are still at opacity 0, so the copper focus ring can't be seen at first (2.4.7 Focus Visible). Measured effective opacity of document.activeElement at t=0 / t=250ms / t=1.75s: WhatsApp and This website 'HOW IT'S BUILT' went 0 / 0 / 1 at 1440, 375 and 1280x620; the contact email link went 0 / 0.74 / 1. The reveal only starts once the element passes 'top 88%', then fades over 1.2s plus the stagger delay. A control focused inside the bottom 12% of the viewport would stay invisible.
suggested_fix: Add a document 'focusin' listener in Reveals: if the target is inside a [data-reveal] element (or its stagger child) that hasn't revealed yet, finish that tween at once (tween.progress(1) or ScrollTrigger.getById(...).animation.progress(1)), or gsap.set the element to opacity 1. A CSS fallback also works: [data-reveal]:focus-within, [data-reveal] > :focus-within { opacity: 1 !important; }.
note: focused control still fading in: pass 2 (focusin completes reveal)

description: The WhatsApp chat demo loops forever with no way to pause, stop or hide it (WCAG 2.2.2, Level A). The GSAP timeline has repeat:-1 and plays whenever it is visible. Hovering doesn't hold it: while the mouse stayed over the demo, the visible bubble count per second read 1,1,2,2,3,3,4,4,4,4,0,1,1,2,2,3. The preview has 0 focusable elements, so focus can't hold it either. The Slides component got hover/focus hold in 43d4a5b; the chat did not.
suggested_fix: Play it once and rest on the finished conversation, with a small 'Replay' button. If it must loop, add a visible Pause/Play toggle (button with aria-pressed and a translated label) in the chat header, and pause on pointerenter and focusin as Slides does.
note: chat plays 3 rounds, holds on hover, rests on the full conversation

description: The auto-advancing slides still have no lasting way to pause or stop (2.2.2 A / 2.2.1). The hold added in 43d4a5b only lasts while a mouse is over the slides or focus is inside them. On touch, pointerType 'touch' is ignored, and iOS Safari doesn't focus a button on tap. Measured at 390 touch: tap '02' with focus not kept → the pressed state went 010 → 001 within 4.6s, so the slide the visitor picked is replaced. Left alone, it cycles 001 → 100 forever. A mouse user who clicks a tab and then moves the pointer away also has the choice overridden. Screen-reader users in browse mode never move focus, so it never holds for them.
file_line: components/projects/Slides.tsx:59-67 (timer), :90-93 (hold only for mouse/focus), :138 (onClick only sets active)
suggested_fix: Treat any explicit tab choice (click, tap or keyboard) as 'stop autoplay': onClick={() => { setActive(i); setAuto(false); }} and gate the timer on auto. Add a Pause/Play button as the first control in the tab row (aria-label 'Pause slideshow' / 'Mettre en pause'). Hold on touchstart too.
verified_evidence: verify-c slides-stop-on-pick: stays on the picked slide

description: Chat demo semantics: who said what is shown only visually (left/right alignment, copper versus graphite bubble). Screen readers get one merged run of text: 'AI agent Hi! Can I book a haircut this week? Hi! Sure. I have Tuesday… Tuesday at 10 please Booked: Tuesday at 10:00… agent.log' (1.3.1). With motion, the bubbles switch between display:none and visibility:hidden, so what's in the accessibility tree changes every ~12s: a snapshot 2.5s in held only the first message. The agent.log lines (English words like 'reply sent' and 'booking saved ✓') have no lang override on /fr (3.1.2).
suggested_fix: Keep a static transcript for assistive tech: an <ol aria-label="Demo conversation"> with visually hidden 'Customer:' / 'Agent:' prefixes (translated), and aria-hidden on the animated visual copy. Add aria-hidden to the typing dots, and lang="en" (or aria-hidden) on the agent.log column.

viewport: 375, 390 (FR; all phone widths with text spacing)
description: Slide captions are cut to 2 lines with an ellipsis (line-clamp-2), so part of the text is lost on screen. At 375 FR, Lead Finder slides 1 and 3 and Clarté slide 2 overflow (scrollHeight 52 > clientHeight 34; slide 1 ends '…un score de 0 à…'); at 390 FR, Lead Finder slides 1 and 3 do. With WCAG 1.4.12 text spacing applied (line-height 1.5, letter-spacing 0.12em, word-spacing 0.16em), every caption at 375 and 390 in both locales is clipped (56 > 38): a 1.4.12 AA failure. The FR tab label '01 · PROSPECTS' also wraps onto 2 lines at 375/390 while its siblings stay on 1.
suggested_fix: Remove line-clamp-2. Keep the reserved min-h-[2lh] (3lh below md) so the frame barely moves, or reserve the height of the longest caption for that slideshow by measuring the captions once.
note: no line clamp; 3 lines reserved on phones

description: Slide tab semantics: the tabs are separate aria-pressed toggle buttons ('01 · Leads, toggle button, pressed') for what is a single-choice set. There's no group name, no aria-controls, and no link to the image or caption they change. They come before the card's h3 in the DOM, so a screen-reader user hears '01 · Website' or '01 · Leads' with no project context (2.4.6 / 1.3.1 best practice). Pressing one changes the image above the buttons, which a screen-reader user can only perceive through the caption live region.
suggested_fix: Wrap the buttons in role="group" with aria-label '<project title> screens' (or use aria-roledescription="carousel" on the slideshow region, following the APG carousel pattern). Keep aria-pressed but add aria-controls pointing at the slide viewport, or switch to aria-current="true" on the active one.
note: tabs grouped and named after the project

description: Alt text repeats the caption. The active image reads 'Lead Finder's dashboard with leads ranked by priority' and then the caption reads 'The dashboard: new leads ranked by priority, each with a transparent 0–100 score'. Clarté: 'The Clarté HQ overview with requests, upcoming lessons and payments', then 'My private dashboard: requests, upcoming lessons and payments…'. Screen-reader users hear the same thing twice. Inactive slides are correctly aria-hidden, so there are no duplicate hidden alts.
suggested_fix: Mark each slide up as a figure whose caption is the <figcaption>, and make the alt describe only what the caption doesn't (e.g. 'Screenshot'), or use alt="" with aria-describedby on the caption.
note: alt describes the image, caption the context; P3

description: The progress bars don't show which slide is current. Earlier slides keep a full copper bar (i < active renders no scale-x-0), and with reduced motion or after a slide's animation ends, the active bar is also full. With '02' active, bars 01 and 02 look the same. The current slide then shows only through label lightness: paper against paper/55, about a 3:1 difference, the same colour and the same weight (1.4.1 / 1.4.11, borderline).
suggested_fix: Show past slides' bars at bg-paper/30 (or empty) so only the active bar is copper. Add a non-colour cue on the active label (font-weight or an underline).
note: past steps faint, only the current step copper

description: The external 'View website ↗' links use target="_blank", and the ↗ is aria-hidden, so assistive tech isn't told the link opens a new tab. The two links also share an accessible name ('View website' / 'Voir le site') but lead to different sites, and the articles have no accessible name to tell them apart. NOTE: content/site.ts in the working tree adds a ui.newTab string, which may already be heading here.
suggested_fix:
Add {t(ui.newTab)} inside each link and aria-labelledby={titleId} on each
. Optionally use aria-label ': View website (opens in a new tab)'.

description: Small text margins in the preview title bar and tabs. The 'Real app screens' / 'Illustrative demo' badge is text-copper/80 at 0.58rem (9.28px) on graphite, giving 4.58:1, only 0.08 above AA. The slug is text-mute at 0.62rem (9.92px) on graphite, 5.47:1. The inactive tab labels were paper/45 at 9.6px, 3.95:1, which is the axe failure; 43d4a5b changed them to paper/55, measured at 5.41:1, which passes. Axe's 'incomplete' contrast items were all in nav/hero; in About, Focus and Projects every other text node measures 5.4:1 or better, composited over the actual background.
suggested_fix: Use full text-copper for the badge (about 6.5:1 on graphite) and bring the 0.58–0.62rem mono labels up to at least 0.65rem.

description:
Missing structure in the card details. In the 'How it's built' panel, the Problem, Solution and How-it-works labels are

elements, so they aren't headings or

s and screen-reader users can't jump between them. The Stack
holds bare spans, which read as one run: 'Next.js TypeScript Supabase Claude API DuckDB Vitest', where 'Claude API DuckDB' is ambiguous. The accordion itself works: aria-expanded, aria-controls, inert and aria-hidden all toggle correctly, and focus stays on the button.
suggested_fix: Render the specs as a <dl>, with each label as a <dt> and the text as a <dd>. Render the stack as <ul role="list"> with an <li> per chip.

viewport: 390x844 touch (any touch device where tapping a button focuses it, e.g. Chrome Android)
description: Tapping a slide tab on a touch screen freezes the slideshow for good. Steps: 390x844 touch, scroll to Lead Finder, tap '02 · DESIGNS'. Observed: the tapped button keeps focus, so onFocus sets held=true. Touch never fires the mouse-only pointerleave that would clear it, and blur never happens. The progress bar stays at scaleX 0 with animation-play-state paused for 12+ s, and it is still paused after scrolling 1500px away and back (tested 18 s later). On Clarté the same tap stops the carousel from ever reaching the dashboard slide. Expected: a tap jumps to that slide and autoplay carries on, or at least resumes after a while or once the card leaves the screen. The empty, paused bar reads as broken.
suggested_fix: Hold on keyboard focus only: onFocus={(e) => e.target.matches(':focus-visible') && setHeld(true)}. Clear the hold when the card leaves the screen (setHeld(false) in the IntersectionObserver callback when !isIntersecting). For touch, restart the countdown on tap instead of holding.
note: hold only on keyboard focus-visible; a tap on a step stops autoplay deliberately

description: Hovering holds the countdown but not the scroll slide's glide. Steps: 1440x900, scroll to Clarté, and while slide 01 · WEBSITE is gliding move the pointer onto the preview. Observed: the progress bar freezes (scaleX 0.16, paused) while the screenshot keeps gliding, translateY going from -124 to -2376px over 6 s of hovering. The visitor who stopped to read watches the page scroll away under the cursor. After the pointer leaves, the bar runs about 9 s more over a page that is already parked at the bottom. The Lead Finder 03 · DEMO slide behaves the same way. Expected: hover pauses the glide along with the bar.
file_line: components/projects/Slides.tsx:111-115 (glide keyed on `playing`, the timer and bar on `advancing` at line 45)
suggested_fix: Drive the glide from `advancing` and make it pausable. Use WAAPI (img.animate([{transform:'translateY(0)'},{transform:`translateY(${-distance}px)`}], {duration: glide, delay: SCROLL_PAUSE, fill:'forwards'})) and call .pause()/.play() alongside the bar, or a GSAP tween you pause and resume. A CSS transition cannot be paused mid-way.

viewport: 1440x900 desktop (the same logic runs on every viewport)
description: Scrolling away from a scroll slide mid-glide and coming back desyncs the glide from the timer, so the slide advances halfway down the page. Steps: 1440x900, let Clarté 01 · WEBSITE play for 6 s, scroll 1400px down (below the 35% threshold), wait 1.2 s, scroll back. Observed: the countdown resumes where it stopped (bar at 0.52), but the image snaps back to the top and glides again from 0. The bar fills while the screenshot is at -1437px of 2921, and the slide switches to the dashboard at about 55% of the page, so the request form at the bottom is never shown. Expected: the glide resumes from where it paused, or the whole slide restarts, glide and timer together.
file_line: components/projects/Slides.tsx:61-69 (the remaining time is kept) vs 111-115 (the transform resets to 0 when !playing)
suggested_fix: Pause the glide and resume it from its current offset (a pausable WAAPI or GSAP tween, as in the hover finding), so both share one clock. Otherwise, reset remaining.current to the full duration whenever the active slide is a scroll slide and becomes visible again.
note: glide/timer desync after scrolling away: pass 2

viewport: 1440x900 desktop, image arriving late (slow network, or delayed 5 s through a route); window resize has the same effect
description: When a scroll slide's screenshot finishes loading after the slide has started, the slide's duration changes mid-slide (8000 -> 11137 ms for Clarté). The progress bar jumps backwards (0.537 -> 0.431) because animation-duration changes under a running animation. The countdown also restarts from the full 11137 ms, so the bar reaches 100% at t=14.5 s and then sits full for about 4.5 s until the slide advances at t=19 s, while the image is still gliding. A window resize while a scroll slide is up re-measures, changes the duration and causes the same jump. Expected: a monotonic bar that stays in step with the advance.
file_line: components/projects/Slides.tsx:57-59 (remaining reset on every duration change), 76 (measure on load/resize), 150 (animationDuration)
suggested_fix: Know the distance before the image loads: pass the capture's intrinsic width and height from content/site.ts, set width/height on the , and compute distance = viewWidth * h / w - viewHeight. If it must change mid-slide, keep the elapsed time (remaining = newDuration - elapsed) and set a negative animation-delay on the bar so it continues from the same fraction.
note: intrinsic sizes for scroll captures: pass 2

viewport: 1440x900 desktop at about 400 kbps (Slow 3G-like CDP throttling); every viewport on a slow connection
description: No loading state: the slide area is a blank white rectangle until the screenshot arrives, and autoplay keeps stepping through slides that haven't loaded. Steps: load /en, apply 400 kbps / 400 ms throttling, scroll to Clarté. Observed: from 0.8 s to 8 s the frame is pure white (slide 01's clarte-laptop-en.webp is 546 KB). At 9 s it auto-advances to 02 while slide 01 has never painted, and at 16 s it goes back to 01, still white. The 20 s run ended without slide 01 completing, while the inactive slide 02 (125 KB) finished first. Every slide in a card is in the viewport under opacity 0, so all of them lazy-load at once and the inactive ones take bandwidth from the visible one. Expected: a dark or skeleton placeholder in the site's palette, and the timer waiting for the current slide's image.
file_line: components/projects/Slides.tsx:96 (bg-white), 61-69 (the timer ignores load state); components/projects/Shot.tsx:27 (loading=lazy on every slide)
suggested_fix: Use bg-ink or bg-graphite with a subtle shimmer until img.complete, and switch to white only for loaded 'contain' stills (e.g. a data-loaded attribute on the slide). Don't let `advancing` be true until the active slide's image has loaded. Give the first slide fetchPriority='high'. Render later slides' src only once the slide before them has loaded, or use loading='lazy' plus decoding on demand.
note: graphite ground until each capture loads

description: No error state for a missing screenshot. Steps: block /projects/clarte-laptop-en.webp, lf-overview.webp or site-en.webp (route.abort), or go offline before scrolling to Projects. Observed: in Lead Finder and Clarté a broken-image icon plus alt text drawn in near-white on the white slide ground, which is almost invisible, inside an otherwise empty frame. Autoplay keeps rotating into the broken slide, and the scroll slide still gets the 8 s default. On card 4 the broken icon and alt text sit top-left in a dark void. Expected: a designed fallback such as the project name and 'Preview unavailable' on the dark ground, with broken slides skipped by autoplay.
suggested_fix: Add an onError handler to Shot that sets a failed flag. Render a fallback block in its place: bg-graphite, the label-mono project slug and a one-line 'preview unavailable' message, with color:transparent on the img so the alt text doesn't overlap. In Slides, skip failed indices when advancing.

description: With reduced motion the scroll slides can't be read past the first screen. Steps: enable reduced motion, go to Lead Finder, click '03 · DEMO', or look at Clarté's '01 · WEBSITE'. description: The datasheet portrait has no loading or error state. description: A latent bug in the media type:'scroll' path that no current project uses. The touch auto-scroll timeline evaluates y: () => -distance() and duration once, the first time it plays. The is loading='lazy', so offsetHeight is usually 0 at that point, which gives a 0 -> 0 tween that never scrolls even after the image loads. Desktop hover re-measures on each pointerenter, so only touch is affected. The 'Hover to scroll' cursor label and this code are dead until a project uses type 'scroll'.
suggested_fix: Call tl.invalidate().restart() from the img's load listener (or ScrollTrigger-style invalidateOnRefresh), or delete the unused 'scroll' media branch.

Opening the Lead Finder panel adds 637px of text at 375 FR (the panel runs from y=356 to 992 in a 667px viewport) and 715px at 320 FR. After reading to the end, you have to scroll a full screen back up to reach the minus toggle, and nothing marks where the panel ends before the next card's links.
suggested_fix: On phones, make the toggle sticky while the panel is open (sticky top-16 bg-ink), or add a small 'Close ↑' control at the end of the panel that collapses it and scrolls the toggle back into view.

description: Scroll slides load very large images into permanently promoted layers, which risks jank or blank frames and tab reloads on iOS. On tablets (768 and up, the laptop source), the Clarté page is 2200x9782 (EN) or 2200x10200 (FR), 21.5-22.4 MP (about 86-90 MB decoded), and the bakery page is 2048x9318 (19.1 MP). Both sit in one card-stack frame next to 2-3 more slides. All of them are in the DOM and load once the card is near. Each tall image has will-change-transform, and the frame (ProjectCard :103) carries will-change-transform on touch too, where nothing tilts. Phones get 729x16235 (11.8 MP) for Clarté, laid out 7238-7572px tall at 375-390. That is one layer about 21,000 device px tall at DPR 3, past WebKit's usual tile and texture budgets.
suggested_fix: Cut the tall captures into 2-3 stacked tiles (e.g. 2200x3200 each), or cap the phone capture at 1170x8000 and the tablet one at 1600 wide. Add will-change only while a slide is active and gliding. Only mount (or set src on) the active and next slide.
note: very tall captures on iOS: asset re-encoding, pass 2 / owner

description: The phone captures are too low-resolution for 3x screens, so text inside the screenshots looks soft. The -m captures are 780px wide (lf-*, site-*), and the Clarté ones only 729 and 710px. At 390 CSS px on a DPR-3 iPhone the frame needs 1020-1170 device px, so images render at 0.62-0.7x. Sideways, the (max-width:767px) source still applies and the frame is 612-679 CSS px wide. The same 780px image is then stretched over 1836-2037 device px (about 0.4x).
suggested_fix: Give the phone source a 3x variant (srcSet with 780w and 1170w plus sizes='(max-width:767px) 92vw'). For landscape phones, pick the source by aspect (orientation: portrait) or use the laptop capture when the width is 600px or more.

description: On a phone held sideways, each Focus drawing fills the screen before the text starts. Below md the art box is aspect-square at full width: 612x612 at 667x375 (1.6 screens) and 679x679 at 740x360 (1.9 screens). Panels are 943-1039px tall, so you scroll almost two screens of looping animation per panel before reaching 'Software' / 'AI' / 'Math', and a panel is never seen whole. At 844x390 the md two-column panels are 393-433px tall, still more than the screen.
suggested_fix: Cap the art height by the viewport: aspect-square max-h-[55svh] w-full, or aspect-[16/9] under (max-height:500px). Better, use the md:grid-cols-2 layout from about 560px wide so the art sits beside the text in landscape.

description: Text inside the AI and Math drawings is unreadable on phones. The SVG is 400 units scaled to 222-292px, so fontSize 10-13 renders at 7-10px. INPUT/HIDDEN/OUTPUT are 8px at 320 and 9px at 375-390. The x/y axis letters and the live readouts 'x = 1.57' and 'f′(x) = 0.00' are 8-10px, and 'f(x) = sin x' is 9-12px. The layer labels are also hard-coded English in the French page ('INPUT / HIDDEN / OUTPUT' under 'IA').
suggested_fix: Scale the SVG text up on small art boxes: fontSize 16-18 in viewBox units, or compute it from the rendered width. Otherwise drop the readouts on phones. Translate the layer labels (entrée / cachée / sortie) or pass them in from site.ts.

description: In the stacked phone list, each Focus panel is taller than the screen. At 375x667 the panels are 685-755px, and at 320x568 they are 671-759px (1.2-1.34 screens). The square art is 270-325px, and the body adds p-8, gap-10 and a 41.6px title. So a sentence of about 25 words costs over a screen of scrolling, the whole section is about 2,400px long, and the title/text/keywords never share the screen with the drawing that goes with them.
suggested_fix: On phones, use an aspect-[4/3] or aspect-[16/10] art box and a tighter body (p-6 gap-6), so a panel fits in about 90svh.

description: At 320 the About facts give most of the row to a mostly empty label column. grid-cols-[8rem_1fr] with gap-6 leaves the values only 120px (EN) or 127px (FR) at text-lg. 'Internships and co-op roles', 'Whatever I haven't learned yet', 'Des stages et des stages coop' and 'Tout ce que je n'ai pas encore appris' each take 3 lines (84px), and even 'Montréal, Canada' and 'Université McGill' wrap to 2. The 128px label column holds 6-10 character labels, and the row reads like a narrow ragged column hugging the right edge.
suggested_fix: Below sm, stack the label above the value (grid-cols-1 gap-2, with the dt as a small mono label), or use grid-cols-[6.5rem_1fr] gap-4 and text-base for the dd.

description: Datasheet values wrap in a narrow column on small phones and in landscape. The rows use grid-cols-[7rem_1fr] gap-4 inside px-5, which leaves 102px (320 EN), 109px (320 FR) and 130px (844x390, where the md column makes the card 300px wide). At 320, 'Lebanon → Montreal', 'Always learning', 'Bâtisseur curieux', 'Liban → Montréal' and 'Toujours en apprentissage' wrap to 2 lines, which breaks the spec-sheet single-line look. The Status dot then floats off to the side of a 2-line value. 'Toujours en apprentissage' still wraps at 360-390 FR.
suggested_fix: Use grid-cols-[5.5rem_1fr] and px-4 below sm (the labels are 4-7 characters), and give the status dot shrink-0.
note: datasheet rows 5.5rem label column below sm

description: Sideways, the portrait alone is taller than the screen, and the About heading is almost 3 screens down. Below md the datasheet is max-w-[500px], so at 667x375 and 740x360 the card is 500x726 and its 5:4 photo is 398px tall, more than the 375 or 360px viewport. The section label and 'Hi, I'm Gregory.' start 969px below the section top at 667x375 (2.6 screens). In portrait, the heading starts 831px down at 375x667 and 843px at 390x844, so tapping About in the menu lands on a bare photo card with no heading. The a11y agent noted the reading-order side; this is the scroll-distance and orientation side.
suggested_fix: On phones, render the SectionHeader before the datasheet (a mobile-only header, or order-first on the text column with the card after the lead paragraph). In landscape, cap the photo box with max-h-[60svh], or use md-style side-by-side columns from about 600px wide when the height is 500px or less.

description: Tapping Menu quickly (3 taps, 60 to 250 ms apart, the way people tap when the first tap seems not to register) leaves the page frozen. The button says 'Close' and aria-expanded is true, the page stays scroll-locked and #main and the footer stay inert, but the drawer has display:none. The user sees the normal page and can't scroll or tap anything in it. Only a tap on the small 'Close' label gets them out. Repro: /en on a phone, tap Menu 3 times fast, try to scroll. Observed (every gap tested): expanded=true, menuDisplay=none, locked=true, mainInert=true, and elementFromPoint over the CTA returns BODY. Expected: the drawer's visibility always matches its open state. Cause: the close tween (gsap.to autoAlpha 0 with an onComplete that sets display:none) is never killed when the menu reopens, so it finishes after the reopen and hides the open menu.
file_line: components/Nav.tsx:116-121 (close tween + onComplete display:none); components/Nav.tsx:86-87 (open path doesn't kill it)
suggested_fix: Call gsap.killTweensOf(el) at the top of both the open and close branches (or give both tweens overwrite:true). In the close onComplete, only set display:none if !openRef.current.
verified_evidence: verify-c menu-triple-tap: consistent open state (expanded, flex, opacity 1, locked)

description: Tapping to skip the boot intro also taps whatever is under your finger. The skip listens for window 'pointerdown' and hides the overlay right away, so the browser then sends the tap's click to the page underneath. Repro: new tab, /en on a phone, tap the lower-left area during the boot. If the tap lands on 'Download CV', the PDF download starts (download event fired). If it lands on 'View projects', the page scrolls to Projects (y=7971). Expected: a tap on the overlay only skips the intro. On desktop, mouse clicks are retargeted and are harmless.
suggested_fix: Skip on the overlay's own 'click' (root.current.addEventListener('click', skip)) instead of window pointerdown. Alternatively, keep pointerdown but add a one-time capture-phase 'click' listener that calls preventDefault()+stopPropagation(), so the tap that skipped the intro can't reach the page.

description: Reload and Back put you one section lower than you were once you're past the Focus section. Reload at y=9600 (Projects) lands at 11446 (Experience). Reload at 13000 (Experience) lands at 14846 (Contact). Switching EN to FR and pressing Back from 5900 (Focus) lands at 8326 (Projects). Positions above Focus restore exactly, and phones restore exactly. Cause: the browser restores the saved scrollY against the layout before JS runs. Focus.tsx then makes the section 1848px taller, and CSS scroll anchoring moves the view by the same amount. With `*{overflow-anchor:none}` injected, restoration was exact (9600 to 9600).
suggested_fix: Add `overflow-anchor: none` to html in globals.css (the page's heights are driven by JS and ScrollTrigger anyway), or reserve the Focus section's height in CSS so the height doesn't change after JS runs. Note: tested on the dev server, where bfcache is off. A production Back may be served from bfcache, but reload is affected either way.

description: Slow loads show nothing at all: no skeleton, no mark, no progress. With Fast-3G and 4x CPU throttling, a first visit shows a plain black screen from 0 to about 9s. The boot overlay is painted, but its mark and copper bar start invisible and only GSAP brings them in. After that comes the 3.3s boot animation. A repeat visit shows an empty dark page for 6 to 9s because the hero is hidden until JS. Visitors can't tell a slow load from a broken page. Absolute times are inflated by dev bundles, but the pattern (nothing shows until JS arrives) doesn't depend on the build.
file_line: components/Boot.tsx:60-68 (.boot-mark starts invisible opacity-0; bar scale-x-0); app/globals.css:123
suggested_fix: Make the pre-JS overlay show progress on its own: render .boot-mark visible and run the copper bar as a CSS keyframe (scaleX 0 to 0.8 over ~2s), then let GSAP take over and finish it. For repeat visits, reveal [data-intro] with a CSS fallback animation after ~1.5s if JS hasn't run yet.

description: After a small scroll, the CTAs are invisible but still clickable. The gate timeline fades .hero-hud-scroll to opacity 0 within the first ~120px of scroll, using opacity only (on purpose, so the CTAs stay in the tab order). 'View projects' and 'Download CV' still receive clicks and taps until the hero ends (~810px at 1440). Repro: scroll to y=300 and tap or click the empty lower-left area. A PDF download starts (download event fired at both 390 and 1440). On desktop the custom cursor ring also grows over blank space.
suggested_fix: Add .set(q('.hero-hud-scroll .pointer-events-auto'), { pointerEvents: 'none' }, 0.15) to the gate timeline (it reverses automatically when scrolling back). Keyboard focus still works because the focusin handler scrolls the hero back to y=0.
verified_evidence: verify-c cta-pointer-events: none at hud opacity 0

description: Scrolling during the ~2.5s intro clips the name. The lines get overflow:hidden for the rise-in, and only the intro's onComplete sets overflow back to visible. If you scroll while the intro is running (repro: load, wait ~0.9s after hydration, scroll to y=260), the gate spreads the letters and the line boxes cut off the outer letters: the 'G' is sliced at x~25 and the 'N' at x~1410. Letters that are still rising are cut off at the bottom. When the intro ends they pop out unclipped, which is a visible jump.
suggested_fix: Clip only vertically while the letters rise, e.g. gsap.set(lines, { clipPath: 'inset(0 -100vw 0 -100vw)' }) instead of overflow:hidden, and clear it in onComplete. Or, in the gate ScrollTrigger's onUpdate, set overflow visible as soon as progress > 0.

description: Using the skip link breaks reload for the rest of the visit. The skip link writes #main into the URL. From then on, a reload always snaps back to the top: scroll to y=6500 and reload, and you land at y=0. Cause: SmoothScroll now scrolls to location.hash once fonts are ready on every load, and this overrides the browser's restored position. The same happens with any hash URL reloaded after scrolling away (/en#projects, then read Contact, then reload, and you're back at Projects).
suggested_fix: Only honour the hash on a fresh navigation: const nav = performance.getEntriesByType('navigation')[0]; if (nav?.type === 'navigate') {...}. Also, the skip link could move focus without writing a hash (onClick: preventDefault, then #main.focus()).
note: saved place beats a leftover #hash on reload

description: Skipping the boot with Space, PageDown or ArrowDown also scrolls the page. The keydown skip unlocks scrolling inside the handler, and the key's default scroll then runs too. Space lands at y=860, so the visitor's first view of the site is the name already torn apart by the gate. ArrowDown lands at y=40. Tab and Enter behave well.
suggested_fix: const skip = (e) => { if (e.type === 'keydown' && [' ', 'PageDown', 'ArrowDown', 'End', 'ArrowUp', 'PageUp', 'Home'].includes(e.key)) e.preventDefault(); tl.progress(1); } (register keydown with passive:false).

description: Switching language always drops you at the top of the other locale, so you lose your place. Repro: open /en#projects, then tap EN/FR. You land on /fr at y=0 (the hero), not on Projects. This happens every time someone switches language mid-page, on /fr too. Deep links with a hash already land correctly now, so the switch could carry the current section along.
suggested_fix: On click, find the section nearest the top of the viewport (for example the last main > section[id] whose top is at or above 40% of the viewport height) and go to `/${other}#${id}`. The full page load is kept on purpose; only the hash is added.

description: Section links never touch the URL or history. go() calls preventDefault and never pushes or replaces state. After clicking About and then Projects, the URL is still /en and history.length hasn't changed, so Back leaves the site (Playwright goBack went to about:blank) instead of returning to the previous section. The address bar can't be copied to share a section, even though hash deep links now work. The skip link is the only thing that writes a hash.
suggested_fix: In go() and toProjects, call history.replaceState(null, '', `#${id}`), which fixes sharing without flooding history. Or use pushState plus a popstate listener that calls scrollToTarget(location.hash || 0) if Back should step through sections.

viewport: 390 (touch), also any width on each repeat load
description: For about 1s after every load (repeat visits, language switches), the header is invisible but can still be tapped. The intro now fades opacity only (no visibility) and has delay 0.9, so the Menu button and EN/FR sit at opacity 0 while still being hit targets. Measured: opacity 0.00 for the first ~1s, with elementFromPoint over Menu returning the button. A tap at the top right in that window opens an invisible menu or switches language.
suggested_fix: Set pointerEvents:'none' in the fromTo's from-state and 'auto' in onStart or when opacity passes 0.5. Or shorten the delay on repeat visits.
note: header pointer-events none during its delayed fade

description: The designed 1.6s ease-out-quart nav scroll never runs. Lenis is created with anchors:true, so its window-level click handler also calls lenis.scrollTo(hash) with the default lerp for every same-page #link. That runs after go() or toProjects have called scrollToTarget(..., {duration:1.6, easing}), and replaces it. Measured trajectory to Projects: 44% of the distance in the first 100ms and 80% by 400ms, settling at ~2.2s. The quart curve would give ~23% and ~68%, done at 1.6s.
suggested_fix: Set anchors:false, since every in-page link already goes through scrollToTarget. Or pass the same {duration, easing} as the anchors option.

description: The nav hides as soon as you use it to go down. Clicking About or Projects from the top scrolls down, the hide-on-scroll-down rule fires, and the header ends at translateY(-88px). Going on to another section means scrolling up first to get the nav back (Playwright couldn't click Contact after About because the header was off-screen). There is also no active-section state (no aria-current or highlight) to confirm where you landed.
suggested_fix: Ignore direction changes while a scroll started by scrollToTarget is running (set a flag in scrollToTarget and clear it in Lenis onComplete), and leave the header shown when it lands. Optionally mark the current section's link with aria-current='location'.
note: header stays while a nav scroll runs

description: With JS off, phones have no navigation. The Menu button renders and looks tappable, but the drawer is class 'hidden' and only JS opens it. After tapping, aria-expanded stays false and the menu stays display:none. The desktop links are hidden below md, so a JS-off phone visitor has a dead control and no way to jump to any section.
suggested_fix: Hide the button under html:not(.js) and show the menu's link list as a plain inline list there. Or make the button an <a href='#mobile-menu'> with a #mobile-menu:target { display:flex } fallback.
note: no-JS phones: failsafe shows content; menu needs JS

description: The sentence renders fully lit before JS arrives, then snaps back to dim. Repro: reload while the Statement is on screen with JS delayed 4s. Before hydration every word is at opacity 1. When SplitText runs, all words not yet reached drop to 0.2 in one frame, so the text visibly 'goes out'. The header is also missing until JS arrives.
suggested_fix:
Give the paragraph a pre-split dim state under html.js (e.g. a class on the

: html.js .statement-text { color: rgb(237 235 230 / .2) }), and set the words' own colour/opacity once split. That way the only change is words lighting up, never the whole block dimming.

description: When the boot halves finish sliding away, the page looks ready but isn't clickable yet. The transparent .boot root (fixed inset-0 z-90) stays until the timeline's onComplete, so for ~0.5 to 0.8s (t≈3.0 to 3.3s) elementFromPoint returns DIV.boot. A desktop click in that window is used up as a 'skip' and does nothing on the page, so the user has to click again.
suggested_fix: Add tl.set(root.current, { pointerEvents: 'none' }, 'split+=0.5') (or right at 'split'), so the page takes input as soon as it's visible.
note: overlay pointer-events none after the split

description: The 404 page doesn't follow the URL's language. /fr/nope shows the English-first 404 (lang='en', 'Page not found.' first, logo links to /en, primary button 'Back to the site' goes to /en), so a French visitor gets English first. global-not-found has no params, but the URL is known on the client.
suggested_fix: Add a tiny inline script: if (location.pathname.startsWith('/fr')) set documentElement.lang='fr-CA', point the logo at /fr and swap which button is primary (e.g. with a data-fr attribute and CSS order).

description: Offline, the language switch throws the visitor onto Chrome's offline error page (chrome-error://chromewebdata/). The switch is a full page load and there's no service worker or cached fallback. Download CV fails the same way. That's acceptable for a portfolio, but it's the only in-page control that can leave the site in a broken state.
suggested_fix: Optional: in the switch's onClick, if (!navigator.onLine) preventDefault and show a small 'You're offline' note next to EN/FR.
